Latest Update: Apple services, including iCloud, App Store, Apple Music, and more, hit by outage

💡 Key Takeaways
  • After a recent slew of tech outages, service disruptions, and flight chaos this week, it’s now Apple customers who are facing technical issues.
  • According to recent reports, the iPhone maker’s System Status page indicates that there are challenges with iCloud’s Account & Sign In services affecting “all people,” which could make the service slow or unavailable.
  • Sources indicate that like all major tech companies, Apple faces outages and other technical challenges affecting its cloud services at times.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a recent slew of tech outages, service disruptions, and flight chaos this week, it’s now Apple customers who are facing technical issues.

According to recent reports, the iPhone maker’s System Status page indicates that there are challenges with iCloud’s Account & Sign In services affecting “all people,” which could make the service slow or unavailable. The App Store, AppleCare on Device, and Apple Music are also experiencing issues, the page indicates.

Sources indicate that like all major tech companies, Apple faces outages and other technical challenges affecting its cloud services at times. However, today’s issues are likely more noticeable to end owners because problems with iCloud can lead to account sign-in problems. This could cause your iPhone to ask for your Apple ID and password, and you could see other attempts to sign in to services with your Apple account information fail.

On Reddit, some folks also noted that they were unable to activate a new iPhone, which is likely related to these ongoing challenges.

According to recent reports, given the recent increase in AI-driven cyberattacks, users across social media have already begun to speculate about the cause. In particular, users are expressing concerns about the Apple outage, as it arrives only days after technical failures at Microsoft led to its cloud systems that power flagship services like Outlook and Teams failing due to cascading software complications.

Similarly, a brief outage of Chase’s banking app this week garnered attention, as did an ongoing partial outage (at the time of publication) of the National Security Agency’s internal classified network, both of which were blamed on software glitches.

So far, none of the outages in the past week have been attributed to cyberattacks, but rather to technical problems.

Apple responded to TechCrunch’s request for comment (which it initially gave to Bloomberg), noting that the outages were caused by an internal patch and not a cyberattack. “Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning. We’re working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible,” the statement read.

After the initial outages were reported, Apple’s status page was updated to include other outages impacting Apple School Manager, iCloud Mail, iCloud Web Apps (iCloud.com), Schoolwork, and the Volume Purchase Program.

By 6 PM ET on Tuesday, the status page revealed all the outages were resolved.

This article was updated after publication with the status of the outages.

#23810. Latest Update: YouTube will start boosting public view counts when you watch on a TV

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (257 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets 📈 Bullish 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: YouTube will start boosting public view counts when you watch on a TV

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (257 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It will estimate co-views based on a ‘privacy-safe statistical model.’.
  • YouTube view counts are about to go up (again) thanks to a newly introduced metric.
  • YouTube thinks that is has been undercounting viewers in group-watching situations, thus not giving creators a true picture of a video's reach.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It will estimate co-views based on a ‘privacy-safe statistical model.’.

YouTube view counts are about to go up (again) thanks to a newly introduced metric. Google's video streaming platform may count more than one person when videos are viewed on a TV, according to an X post from YouTube Creator Insider. These extra "co-views" will apply to long form, Shorts, and Live videos, for TV views only.

YouTube thinks that is has been undercounting viewers in group-watching situations, thus not giving creators a true picture of a video's reach. The goal with the latest metric, the platform wrote, is to "[align] with TV industry standards — including how traditional broadcast and streaming networks estimate the total number of people exposed to content.".

How, you might wonder, will YouTube know who else is watching besides the account-holder? The platform emphasized that it won't use "devices, cameras, microphones or anything like that." Rather, views will be estimated using a "privacy-safe statistical mode" based on things like demographic patterns and viewing times, calibrated against real-life testing data. YouTube didn't share any other methodology details.

The upcoming system will show higher public view counts and watch times for videos, giving creators more data to guide their channel strategy, brand pitches and more (the co-view parameter won't be retroactively applied). What it won't get them is more ad money. "Co-views don't impact ad revenue or YPP thresholds," YouTube Creator Insider wrote. "Creator earnings, AdSense payouts and YouTube Partner Program eligibility remain based on Qualified Views and Watch Hours.".

#23808. Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors

Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (574 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both firm code and code that is provided by each customer.
  • ReportURI researcher Scott Helme remarked the delivery mechanism wasn’t a CDN cache poisoning attack, which uses HTTP to cause a CDN to cache harmful responses.
  • “We don’t know how the attacker got write access to so many unrelated customer projects: a compromised Optimizely system, a compromised credential with cross-customer access, or something else,” ReportURI Helme wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both firm code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript.

ReportURI researcher Scott Helme remarked the delivery mechanism wasn’t a CDN cache poisoning attack, which uses HTTP to cause a CDN to cache harmful responses. Instead, the attack relied on Optimizely’s legitimate infrastructure, including its domains, to serve the tainted code. Optimizely’s own customer JavaScript for the www.optimizely.com and login.optimizely.com URLs were also affected.

“We don’t know how the attacker got write access to so many unrelated customer projects: a compromised Optimizely system, a compromised credential with cross-customer access, or something else,” ReportURI Helme wrote. “That’s for Optimizely to explain.”.

Optimizely representatives didn’t respond to questions sent by email.

It has been revealed that the scripts were named track.js, and all four components became active at the same time. Devices that received the malicious code responded differently depending on their platform and what they were doing on the final page delivering it. Actions performed included:.

It has been revealed that 1. Crypto wallet address swapping. The script searches for wallet addresses for nine different cryptocurrencies and, when found, replaces them with one of the attacker’s. ReportURI said funds have already been stolen from some people whose devices ran the code.

Industry observers note that 2. Card skimming. The script watches HTTP requests for payment card numbers, expiry dates, and CVVs. When all three are present, it sends them to https://1688360.cc/card.php. Cards entered in hosted payment iframes such as Stripe and Adyen were unaffected.

According to recent reports, 4. The DarkSword and Coruna exploit kits for iOS. The kits are delivered through a file named boot.js served from 5vobauua3ojpklx.icu and eil786npto9u5bq.icu. The file delivers a hidden iframe that contains an exploit chain tailored to the iOS version being used. Coruna can infect iOS versions 13 to 17. DarkSword can infect versions 18.x. A separate chain for iOS 26 fingerprints devices but doesn’t appear to do anything else. Earlier this month, researchers saw hackers possibly linked to the Kremlin attempting to deliver DarkSword through multiple vectors, including a compromised web analytics service.

It has been revealed that the list of sites that ReportURI found delivering the malicious scripts numbers 178, and as noted, includes many massive names. It’s unclear if the list is exhaustive. Helme mentioned in an interview that “Ars wasn’t affected as far as we saw, and I haven’t seen any other indications it was.” Website administrators can check both the ReportURI post and this one from security firm Cynet for indicators of compromise.

At the moment, there’s no information available on how successful the exploit chains were in installing the payloads. Beyond the bare-bones details above, more precise information about what versions of iOS were susceptible was also unavailable. These sorts of gaps are common in breaking news concerning mass malware attacks, because it takes time for researchers to sift through the evidence. Readers are encouraged to check back as upcoming developments come to light.

The indicators may help end consumers determine if they are affected, but the skill required is likely out of reach for many.

FAA suspends installation of router that led to a ground stop of flights across the US

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The router malfunctioned and flooded other routers with data, prompting the FAA to order the ground stop.
  • The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has suspended the installation of a router model made by Hewlett-Packard Enterprise-owned Juniper Networks, which was part of its modernization efforts.
  • If you'll recall, Transport Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the ground stop on old hardware the first time he spoke about the event.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The router malfunctioned and flooded other routers with data, prompting the FAA to order the ground stop.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has suspended the installation of a router model made by Hewlett-Packard Enterprise-owned Juniper Networks, which was part of its modernization efforts. As The New York Times reports, the agency believes the router played a major role in the issue that caused it to order a ground stop for all flights in the US on November 13. In addition to suspending new installations, it has also disabled more than 60 routers that had already been installed.

If you'll recall, Transport Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the ground stop on old hardware the first time he spoke about the event. But Duffy revealed a day later that the concern was connected to the modernization of America's aviation facilities.

Recent findings suggest that he stated a contractor from tech manufacturer L3Harris was working on switching telecommunication lines from old copper wires to fiber and on installing the upcoming router at an FAA site in El Dorado, Arkansas. That router started flooding other routers in the air traffic control system with data. Another router in Amarillo, Texas had also gone haywire, and the FAA responded by disabling both of them.

The agency stated the router was tested for a year before installations started. "Sixty-eight times it worked well," he sad at a news conference. "This one router started to broadcast into our network, and it started to overload the network." In aviation, routers are used to transmit data, including radar feeds, flight aims and weather information.

Despite knowing that it was the router that caused the problem, FAA administrator Bryan Bedford said they still don't know what triggered it. The Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee's Democratic members are urging the agency to find out why it had malfunctioned. They also asked the FAA to report to Congress on how it's going to prevent the same thing from happening in the future.

Duffy noted he was told by national security agencies that the issue wasn't caused by a cyberattack, but he still asked the FBI to be part of the team analyzing the router from Arkansas. The Transport Secretary has also renewed his calls for Congress to approve an additional $50 billion in funding to modernize America's air traffic control system. "I would just tell you, the longer we stay on an old rickety network, the less safe it becomes," he said. "We do have to get this work done. Otherwise, staying on the old system for longer is going to mean more risk as opposed to fixing the system, and you're going to reduce the risk.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Organisers say up to 10,000 people could join next round of demonstrations as US president arrives for Asean summit.

Asean and Apec summits – as it happened.

Hundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against Donald Trump in Manila, as the US president arrived in the city for a leaders’ summit.

Organisers claimed as many as 10,000 people would be joining protests against Trump in the capital of the Philippines on Tuesday, where he is attending the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit. The crowds were expected to try to march to the summit site.

Authorities have arrested nearly 300 people in widespread protests held in the days leading up to the summit, with large parts of the capital closed off and tight security in place.

In a recent development, some burned effigies of Trump and faced off with police officers armed with batons and shields. Slogans on placards called the American leader the world’s “No 1 terrorist” in protests held on Monday.

Demonstrators angry at the cost of living and energy shock caused by the Iran war, and the new US-led Pax Silica initiative on AI and critical minerals, tried to reach the summit at the Philippine International Convention Center on Monday, but were blocked by police.

Pax Silica has sparked tensions in the Philippines over plans to build a tech hub outside Manila that critics say will affect water and energy supplies, and displace members of the Ayta Indigenous community.

Large sections of central Manila were closed to the public as part of the security cordon and public holidays put in place for the Asean summit.

After departing from Fairbanks in Alaska, Trump emerged from Air Force One at Ninoy Aquino International airport at 5.54pm local time (0954 GMT), live video demonstrated.

Industry observers note that trump will meet with the leaders of Australia, Japan and India on Tuesday night before heading to Shenzhen in China on Wednesday. There he will attend the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit and hold trilateral talks with China’s president, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin of Russia.

The backlash against Trump follows the ousting of the boss of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, and allegations members of the US administration, including the commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, knew about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Trump’s delegation was expected to include Elon Musk.

Protest leader Renato Reyes blamed the arrests in Manila on the heavy handed response of the government on the president, Ferdinand Marcos Jr, calling Monday the largest single day of police arrests since Marcos came to office in 2022.

According to recent reports, “It is really crazy that the Philippine government is rolling out the red carpet for someone who has been so flatly rejected by the American people,” Reyes mentioned. “Trump started a war that devastated the global economy and pushed oil prices in the Philippines to historic highs. It has caused untold suffering on the Filipino people.

“So, yes, Trump will have to pay for his crimes and he will have to be answerable, not just to the American people, but to the people of the world.”.

The Philippine national police mentioned some officers were injured during confrontations with demonstrators opposed to the summit, including when objects were allegedly thrown at officers.

Pax Silica will include a technology hub planned at New Clark City in Tarlac, about 100km from Manila.

Intended to bolster western stocks of AI technology and reduce “excessive dependencies” on single source supply chains, including from China, Pax Silica will provide chips and critical minerals to 26 participating signatory governments.

Amnesty International stated demonstrations should not be forcibly or violently dispersed.

Sources indicate that “Reports of arrests during the protests demand immediate scrutiny,” Amnesty’s director for the Philippines, Ritz Lee Santos III, stated. “Authorities must explain the specific grounds for each arrest and any continued detention. Anyone detained solely for peacefully exercising their rights must be released immediately.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google is expanding the rollout of Tasks, a toggle in Gemini that converts the chatbot into a more active helper.

Unlike Gemini’s Chat, which merely allows users to talk to Google’s AI assistant for informational purposes, Tasks empowers the app to complete basic secretarial functions, deputizing it as a kind of personal assistant.

How, specifically, can you use it? Google says that the app can call businesses and book appointments on users’ behalf; it can also complete purchases for them via Google Pay, and even sign into websites securely if prompted to do so.

According to recent reports, in a blog post, Josh Woodword, VP of Gemini, claims to have recently used the feature to call local car dealerships to schedule a service appointment for his family’s minivan. He says he also used it to analyze his electrical bill.

Getting the function up and running is easy. Customers merely flip a toggle within the app from Chat to Tasks, which enables the feature. Users can also send texts to Gemini or call the app to give it commands.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It would act as a sovereign city state free from things like laws and governments.

It has been revealed that oculus founder and Oxytocin booster Palmer Luckey is touting a new project that combines some of his favorite things like wacky projects and libertarianism. SLAB is an informal initiative for a floating "seastead" designed to last a thousand years that would act as a sovereign state to avoid pesky laws that "cripple" corporations, Luckey mentioned.

In a recent development, an initial AI render depicts a massive artificial island built high above the sea with what looks like office buildings, apartments, refineries... and is that a data center at the top left?

"At a time when most of the seasteading community wanted to escape the US and smoke pot, this was the one project explicitly designed to make America stronger, a relief valve for ill-considered or outdated rules and regulations," Luckey wrote in a post that must be read to be believed.

You may have questions like "wtf is seasteading" and "isn't this just a floating AI data center?" That confusion is understandable, as it uses language and ideas around far-out moonshot concepts that may not be familiar to normal, non-tech-billionaires.

Selling Oculus to Facebook in 2014 gave me money for helicopter flight lessons and developing a seastead called SLAB with a 1,000 year design life.

The goal was to be cheaper than land and absent state/local laws that cripple critical American industries like metal processing,... pic.twitter.com/aJkd0eOgLF.

— Palmer Luckey (@PalmerLuckey) November 18, 2026.

It has been revealed that the idea with seasteading is that if you build a floating structure far enough out in the ocean, you can create your own city-state and make whatever laws you want. The concept has been touted for years by several tech bros including Peter Thiel and Joe Lonsdale. However, the only real seastead you may have heard about was Sea Island that the piracy site Pirate Bay eyed at one point as a base of operations.

"The goal was to be cheaper than land and absent state/local laws that cripple critical American industries like metal processing, medical research/treatment, desalination, oil refining [and] chemical engineering," noted Luckey. "[W]hile it still has a long way to go, there has been significant progress towards my goal of reviving manifest destiny and westward expansion.".

It has been revealed that that raises even more questions! Like, why is Luckey talking about manifest destiny? And what kind of medical research needs to be done at sea beyond the reach of laws? In any case, Luckey, who runs the defense contract firm Anduril and plans on breeding military dogs, noted he wanted to get this SLAB info out now as he was being asked about it by reporters (who later identified themselves as Liz Hoffman and Reed Albergotti, both from Semafor).

Palmer stated that the journalists "plan on calling SLAB my upcoming floating AI datacenter project." However, he offered a riposte that may be the most cringe thing you'll read today: "It is way cooler than that, way older than that, and I hate looking like a hype-chasing consensus loser, so now you have to read this tweet.".

  • Rubio acknowledged that "people are fearful" the spate of outages, which included all flights being grounded in the US and widespread disruptions to banking, Apple and Microsoft services, could be linked or part of a plot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Watch: Marco Rubio notes recent tech outages are 'completely unrelated' to one another.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed widespread concerns online that the series of recent tech outages in the past week are connected, telling reporters there was "zero evidence" of any link.

Rubio acknowledged that "people are fearful" the spate of outages, which included all flights being grounded in the US and widespread disruptions to banking, Apple and Microsoft services, could be linked or part of a plot.

"We are not under systemic attack," he stated. "These events, one has nothing to do with the other, they are not inter-related.".

Cyber-security experts have agreed that there is no evidence linking the outages, and many of the issues appear due to updates to old infrastructure.

In the past week, there has been a massive Microsoft outage, an apparent tech glitch which grounded all US flights for hours, and issues for the National Security Agency, outages affecting the biggest US banks and Apple.

Every affected company or agency has stated the concern was not cyber-related and not the work of an outside actor.

Rubio's comments came hours after US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton also addressed the issue, telling Fox News the outages were not the product of a cyber-attack. He explained "lots of institutions" are patching or upgrading systems, which has caused some disruption.

Rubio was asked whether the Trump administration was concerned public fears could lead to stockpiling or a run on the banks.

He stated the best way to combat such fears was for the US government to share everything they know with the American people.

"Every indicator we have is that every single one of these events has an explanation or a cause that has nothing to do with a cyber-criminal, has nothing to do with a hostile actor or another country," he said.

Technology-related disruptions have happened almost daily since Thursday, when a Microsoft outage disrupted many of its services, including email.

In a recent development, the next day, the US Federal Aviation Administration halted flights across the US for more than four hours with a rare national ground stop. It was the longest halting of flights since the 11 September 2001 attacks on the US.

The US transport secretary mentioned the glitch was technical and caused by a copper wire upgrade and outdated equipment.

On Monday, a United Airlines technology failure delayed about 150 flights and a JPMorgan Chase software problem disrupted service at the biggest and most utilised banks in the US.

Both United and Chase remarked a software issue was behind the glitch.

Apple users were impacted by outages affecting iCloud and Apple Pay on Tuesday. The manufacturer said the cause was not a cyber-attack but the outage was triggered by an an internal upgrade.

The same day, a highly classified network used by the US National Security Agency (NSA) for internal communications also went offline for a period of time.

Passengers wait to check in at Los Angeles International Airport as flights resume after being grounded for several hours on November 13 due to a major communications outage.

Cybersecurity experts say there is no evidence connecting the Microsoft, airline, and bank disruptions from the last five days.

Kris Beevers, CEO and co-founder of the network and infrastructure management manufacturer NetBox Labs, acknowledged the circulating theories on social media linking the barrage of outages.

"There is no conspiracy here," he told the BBC.

"There is something more ordinary, and more notable to understand: the infrastructure that runs the world is changing faster than ever, and change is risk. Much of it is 30 to 40 years old, with decades of technical debt, and it's now being asked to change very swiftly.".

Beevers remarked AI is only part of the story.

"It's putting more strain on these legacy networks, and it's also creating real urgency around security," he stated.

"Our customers are the amazing teams behind these networks at airlines, banking, energy, and retail who are essentially doing heart surgery on a global scale to get these networks back up and running swiftly.".

Vice President of Threat Intelligence for Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, Sherrod DeGrippo, remarked: "What this week really underscores is how tightly coupled, and fragile, our core digital infrastructure is, where a single software bug or router failure can cascade nationwide.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Republicans' losses in the US midterm elections have exposed a feud within the far right in Germany.
  • A rare public disagreement between Alternative for Germany (AfD) leaders over immigration reveals who is winning the battle for the party's future.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here is a roundup of the top news stories from and about Germany on Wednesday, November 18, 2026:.

The Republicans' losses in the US midterm elections have exposed a feud within the far right in Germany.

A rare public disagreement between Alternative for Germany (AfD) leaders over immigration reveals who is winning the battle for the party's future.

Watch below for more on the rift among AfD politicians.

Germany's governing coalition has agreed to reduce electricity tax for households and businesses.

The cut will lower the electricity tax rate for 2027 to the European minimum level.

The agreement between Chancelor Friedrich Merz's conservative CDU/CSU and his junior coalition partner, the center-left Social Democrats (SPD), was reached after multiple failed attempts.

Funding for the tax cut has only been secured for the year 2027, but the coalition stressed in a summary document of the agreement that it aimed to achieve a "permanent reduction." An extension is contingent on finding a way to fund it into 2028, according to the paper.

The coalition partners said that the tax cut will be funded by surplus funds from subsidies under the renewable energy bill, as the government anticipates lower demand for renewable energy subsidies next year.

The government is also to introduce a three-month cap on fuel prices in January.

The CDU/CSU and SPD promised in their 2025 coalition deal to cut taxes for all consumers, but initially only applied a reduction for industry, agriculture and forestry. Wednesday's agreement extends cuts to households and to businesses that did not qualify for the initial reduction.

Germany has some of the highest electricity prices in Europe, in part thanks to shocks following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine and by the United States and Israel's war with Iran.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Wednesday agreement still needs to be incorporated into the 2027 budget. The budget must then be cleared by the parliamentary budget committee, with the lower house of parliament, the Bundestag, expected to give final approval on November 27.

The 2027 federal budget proposal marks a major shift in German fiscal policy, with Berlin taking on increasing debt, citing the need to finance repairs to the country's crumbling infrastructure, carry out the energy transition and expand and modernize the military.

Germans are seemingly requesting days off work to play GTA 6 ahead of the videogame's Thursday release, according to data from the HR software company Personio.

GTA 6 is part of the popular open-world, action-adventure series  "Grand Theft Auto," in which the player can explore a city, commit crimes outside, and complete hours worth of missions.

The latest installment has been eagerly awaited by gamers for 13 years, having been subject to two delays and multiple leaks.

The Munich-based personnel software provider Personio said that Germany saw 38% more requests for days off than usual for the launch of GTA 6, and a 58% in requests for compensatory time off for overtime hours worked.

However, economists do not expect the rush to play the long-awaited game to have any impact on the German economy.

"The economy won't collapse because of GTA, just because some people decide to take a bit of time off," media economist Jörg Müller-Lietzkow was cited by ZDF as saying.

Real net household incomes in Germany are rising again following a period of high inflation, according to a report from the German economics research institute DIW Berlin.

The report revealed that overall income satisfaction has risen significantly as more and more people in Germany are managing to save.

However, the rise has not yet offset earlier losses from high inflation rates in 2022 and 2023, the institute said.

Incomes have grown by an average of nearly one-third since 1995, but inequality has risen significantly — while top incomes have risen by over 50%, those in the middle of the curve have risen by around a quarter and those at the lower end have largely remained stagnant.

DIW Berlin warned that the long-term risk of falling into poverty has risen to 17%.

However, the report's author stressed that the increase in inequality was due to a shift over a longer period and it had not significantly widened in recent years.

"While income inequality in Germany has risen over the long term, it has remained largely stable in recent years," DIW Berlin researcher Markus Grabka said.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz left Tuesday night's coalition talks on an electricity tax cut out of frustration, German tabloid newspaper Bild reported on Wednesday.

Bild cited participants of the coalition meeting as saying that Merz left the talks in Berlin around midnight local time (2300 UTC) over demands made by his CDU/CSU conservative bloc's junior coalition partners, the center-left Social Democrats (SPD).

Before leaving, Merz said "I'm not putting up with this anymore," according to Bild. He later returned to talks, reportedly after speaking to Markus Söder, who leads the Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party to Merz's own Christian Democrats (CDU).

The coalition ultimately agreed upon a reduction in the electricity tax for households and businesses, bringing the rate for 2027 to the European minimum level.

According to Bild, the SPD had insisted on guaranteeing funding for the measure well beyond 2027.

The tax cut is to be funded by surplus funds from subsidies under the renewable energy bill and its extension is contingent on finding a way to fund it into 2028, according to a summary paper of an agreement reached between the two coalition factions.

Bild cited sources close to Merz as saying that the talks had been very difficult and intricate, with the CDU arguing that the matter could have been resolved within an hour, rather than extending deep into the night.

The two parties have regularly been at odds over key policy questions, particularly around budget and taxation concerns.

Police were called to the lost and found for Munich's S-Bahn suburban rail network after a live lobster was found on one of the trains.

The lobster, weighing some 3 kilograms (around 6.6 pounds), was found in a Styrofoam box by S-Bahn workers on Tuesday morning.

He was initially treated with a saline solution and given the nickname "Günni.".

Police determined that the crustacean had initially been purchased from a wholesale market for hospitality and retail in Munich and escorted it back to the point of sale.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul is visiting Armenia and Azerbaijan on Wednesday.

He is set to make his way to Yerevan, Armenia after his visit to the Azerbaijani capital, Baku.

Discussions were to focus on implementing a joint strategic agenda signed by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev in July, according to the ministry.

The leaders were also to discuss the supply of natural gas and crude oil from Azerbaijan.

They were also to touch on the peace process between Armenia and Azerbaijan, which fought wars over the Nagorno-Karabakh territory in 2020 and 2023.

The ministry cited Wadephul as saying Berlin aimed to capitalize on the "positive momentum" between Baku and Yerevan that had developed since the 2025 peace summit in Washington.

Wadephul stated that he also aims to examine Russia's influence in the southern Caucasus.

"In the South Caucasus too, we are seeing Russia try to retain its influence — at the expense of the people and their future," the minister mentioned on Tuesday before embarking on a flight to the region.

Armenia and Azerbaijan were part of the former Soviet Union and Russia maintains significant influence in the region.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Germany's Constitutional Court has rejected an appeal brought by the populist Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason (BSW) against the February 2025 federal election result, dashing the party's hopes it could trigger a recount that would allow it to enter parliament.

The BSW party, formerly known as the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance after the name of its founder, narrowly failed to reach the 5% threshold to enter the lower house of parliament, the Bundestag.

Having received 4,981% of the vote, it would have needed just 9,529 more votes to enter the chamber.

The BSW maintained that there had been an error in the vote count and that the party could be assigned some 35 seats.

If the party were to enter parliament, a rearrangement of seats could also threaten the majority held by the current ruling coalition made up of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservative CDU/CSU alliance and the center-left Social Democrats.

"Everything points to the conclusion that Merz is an illegitimate chancellor and that the current Bundestag is not composed in accordance with the constitution," party founder Sahra Wagenknecht told Germany's DPA news agency before the court published its ruling.

"Without access to the actual ballots, it is impossible to provide further evidence or indications of counting errors to the detriment of the BSW.".

She mentioned that if the court were to rule against the party's appeal, this would be a "slap in the face of democracy.".

Yet another satellite tech giant is jockeying for a rocket—but this one makes sense

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1198 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced Tuesday that it is seeking to buy Italian rocket-maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion in a transaction aimed at creating Europe’s first true vertically integrated end-to-end space organization.
  • According to recent reports, the announcement came as an all-cash voluntary tender offer from an Italian subsidiary of ICEYE to Avio’s shareholders, led by the Italian defense conglomerate Leonardo.
  • Avio builds the Vega C rocket, a solid-fueled launcher designed to carry up to 3.3 metric tons (7,300 pounds) of payload to low-Earth orbit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced Tuesday that it is seeking to buy Italian rocket-maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion in a transaction aimed at creating Europe’s first true vertically integrated end-to-end space organization.

According to recent reports, the announcement came as an all-cash voluntary tender offer from an Italian subsidiary of ICEYE to Avio’s shareholders, led by the Italian defense conglomerate Leonardo. Avio said its board of directors “has taken note of the notice” from ICEYE and is considering the purchase offer.

Avio builds the Vega C rocket, a solid-fueled launcher designed to carry up to 3.3 metric tons (7,300 pounds) of payload to low-Earth orbit. The Vega C has flown successfully seven times in eight attempts since 2022. It is a follow-on to an earlier version of the Vega rocket that amassed a 20-for-22 record since debuting in 2012.

Sources indicate that ICEYE is, by far, the most successful space startup in Europe, where access to private capital, regulatory barriers, and fragmented markets often hinder startup growth, according to a recent report from the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development. ICEYE’s valuation stands at more than $12 billion after the manufacturer’s most recent fundraising round in June.

In a statement, ICEYE said it wants to join forces with Avio to meet Europe’s need for “sovereign space and defense capabilities.” ICEYE manufactures and operates its own satellites for radar surveillance and sells data to commercial customers and national governments, including Ukraine, which uses ICEYE imagery for targeting and tracking Russian troop movements.

“Governments need control of their critical space infrastructure, and Europe needs it most,” said Rafal Modrzewski, CEO and co-founder of ICEYE. “Avio has built the launch and propulsion capability Europe relies on. With ICEYE’s long-term capital behind it, we can integrate the supply chain, grow output and strengthen the European programs that already depend on it. Together we can build, launch and operate sovereign space systems end-to-end, made in Europe for governments across the world.”.

Avio oversees the consortium of European companies that produces the Vega C rocket and conducts final assembly of Vega C rocket stages at its factory near Rome. For most of the Vega program’s history, Avio handed the rockets to French launch provider Arianespace, which managed marketing, sales, and launch day operations in French Guiana. Avio recently took over those responsibilities to bring the entire Vega C operation in-house.

ICEYE has built and released 84 radar reconnaissance satellites, providing routine overhead imagery of locations around the world, even during darkness or cloud cover. In addition to its commercial satellite fleet, ICEYE has sold turnkey satellites directly to national governments, including Finland, Poland, Germany, Sweden, Portugal, Greece, and the Netherlands.

Recent findings suggest that last month, ICEYE revealed a partnership with Nokia, another Finnish company, to develop a low-Earth orbit satellite constellation to support European connectivity needs, particularly in the defense and security sectors. Ukraine’s Ministry of Defense announced a preliminary agreement, saying it intends to work with ICEYE and Nokia on the constellation, days after Ukraine reported upcoming restrictions on its access to Starlink and Starshield broadband services offered by SpaceX.

In a recent development, “Modern warfare has proven that reliable communications are a matter of national security,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. “We must all rely on capabilities that we can control.”.

Industry observers note that there’s a long way to go before ICEYE and Nokia can start deploying their constellation, but their goal is to begin launching 50 satellites per year starting in 2028. The companies have not disclosed expected figures for throughput and latency on the network, or a total number of satellites for global or regional coverage. Depending on altitude, it would likely require hundreds or thousands of satellites. SpaceX has more than 11,000 operating satellites in its Starlink constellation today.

Sources indicate that what is clear, however, is that ICEYE’s future radar and broadband satellites will need rides to space, and Avio’s Vega C rocket needs business. The primary customer for Vega C is the European Space Agency, and the rest of the rocket’s future schedule is largely filled with satellites from European national governments. Vega C’s purely commercial business line is thin.

Through the proposed transaction, ICEYE says it would secure more access to launch services, and Avio would receive investment for higher production and more frequent flights of the Vega rocket family, which averages fewer than three per year.

The most recent data indicates a dedicated Vega C launch sells for approximately $55 million, just shy of the commercial price for a much more powerful dedicated SpaceX Falcon 9. Nearly all of ICEYE’s satellites, except for the first-view demo spacecraft, have introduced on Falcon 9 rideshare missions, which SpaceX intends to phase out after 2028. SpaceX sold rideshare launch slots for satellites of ICEYE’s size and mass for about $700,000. After accounting for potential savings after ICEYE’s potential purchase of Avio, an ICEYE satellite might be able to launch on Vega C for two to three times that price.

Avio and the European Space Agency are jointly funding the development of a latest version of Vega, the Vega E, which replaces the top part of Vega C with a new higher-performing methane-fueled upper stage. ESA and Avio also signed a nearly $50 million contract last year to begin designing a reusable upper stage similar in concept and appearance to SpaceX’s Starship, although much smaller. The idea is to complete early design work on the reusable upper stage as a potential replacement for Vega E.

According to recent reports, business results seem to bear out the benefits of combining launch and satellite services under one roof. SpaceX’s Starlink network and Falcon 9 rocket would not have been as successful without the other. Rocket Lab, the No. 2 US launch company by launch rate, rapidly branched out into satellite manufacturing after establishing the reliability of its Electron rocket. Pretty much every US launch provider has a role in satellite production or in-space services, or plans to, except for United Launch Alliance.

According to recent reports, the coming launch crunch precipitated by SpaceX’s plans to retire the Falcon 9 has underscored the importance of assured access to space. SpaceX is prioritizing Starship launches for its own Starlink network and future Starmind AI satellites.

Sources indicate that one of SpaceX’s competitors in the satellite broadband business, AST Space Mobile, unveiled last week that it is developing its own rocket to launch its communications network. It has launched most of its satellites to date on Falcon 9. Another tech giant, Cowboy Space, aims to put orbiting data centers into space, bringing it into competition with SpaceX’s Starmind initiative. Cowboy Space, too, recently announced it was working on its own rocket.

There are reasons to disbelieve both companies’ launcher aims. Neither has any rocket development experience, and both are targeting first flights in 2028, a bewilderingly fast path to the launch pad. There are reasons to be skeptical of ICEYE and Avio, too, but if they do join forces, the combined organization would boast established satellite and rocket production lines and backing from European governments seeking to reclaim sovereignty amid fraying ties with the United States.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Host city offers showcase of China’s rise into a confident and innovative power central to global economy.
  • In a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colour spectrum – cyan and violet, cyber green, China’s national scarlet and gold – repeatedly flashing the words “Apec 2026”.
  • The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is a dream showcase for one of China’s most advanced cities, and the country’s leader, Xi Jinping, is basking in its neon glow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Host city offers showcase of China’s rise into a confident and innovative power central to global economy.

In a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colour spectrum – cyan and violet, cyber green, China’s national scarlet and gold – repeatedly flashing the words “Apec 2026”.

The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is a dream showcase for one of China’s most advanced cities, and the country’s leader, Xi Jinping, is basking in its neon glow.

On the sidelines, a series of high-profile bilateral meetings and the announcement of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin have cemented Xi’s status as an agenda setter on the global stage.

The broader Apec summit, meanwhile, provides an opportunity for China to present itself as a steward of multilateralism against what it terms “unilateralism and protectionism” – that is to say, trade measures taken against Beijing by countries such as the US.

All this is set against the futuristic backdrop that is Shenzhen, a city that perhaps better than no other embodies China’s rise into a confident, technologically innovative power central to the global economy.

A photo display in the Apec media centre charts Shenzhen’s transformation from sparsely populated marshland, calling it “a miracle in the history of world development created by the Chinese people”.

“[Xi] wants people to go home Chinamaxxing,” stated Prof Astrid Nordin, of King’s College London. “Shenzhen is itself part of the message. It’s a showcase of Chinese technological and economic achievements, and of China’s claim that it offers opportunities for prosperity in a world increasingly characterised by uncertainty and conflict.”.

Like the light show, the summit is being carefully coordinated. The Financial Times cited people familiar with the matter as saying it would be one of the most tightly controlled in the organisation’s history, with leaders having to travel to a state guesthouse beside Shenzhen’s tiger safari park to meet Xi. The paper remarked diplomats had grumbled that the format “seems designed to reduce the free-flowing discussion characteristic of prior editions”.

Setting out its expectations for the summit, China’s foreign ministry has mentioned it looks forward to “practical results in key areas such as trade, connectivity, digital economy, AI and so on”.

Already, Xi has announced trade wins with Canada’s Mark Carney, extending remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products by two years in exchange for tariff relief on Canadian pork, fish and seafood exports.

A meeting with Papua Fresh ⁠Guinea’s leader, meanwhile, demonstrated how Beijing’s geopolitical priorities have been absorbed and reflected by its allies, with James Marape recounting to Xi how he had closed Taiwan’s office in his country despite domestic challenges in doing so.

The most important meeting will be between Xi and Trump. The leaders of the world’s two superpowers are expected to tackle a broad range of problems including AI and trade. In a move that could strain the fragile tariff truce that the two leaders first agreed last year, the Trump administration stated on Monday it would further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips.

Christopher Adams, a senior adviser at the law firm Covington who was at the centre of trade negotiations with China for the Obama and first Trump administrations, said: “The trade truce may increasingly look like a ceasefire in a war where major combat operations remain on hold but skirmishes are escalating to the point where the line between peace and war is blurred.

“I don’t see pressure to announce a further extension of the trade truce in Shenzhen. If a significant extension is declared, that would be an upside surprise.”.

Recent findings suggest that china has not hesitated to leverage Apec’s multinational platform in service of its arguments. A commentary by the state news agency Xinhua on Tuesday said: “Amid deepening geopolitical rivalries and growing global divisions, [China’s hosting] sends a clear signal that great-power competition need not be a zero-sum game, and that one country’s development need not come at the expense of another.”.

The chair of the Apec senior officials’ meeting, Chen Xu, stated Beijing had made trade “openness” a key focus of its Apec year and looked forward to “achieving more practical outcomes on the trade front”.

The much anticipated trilateral summit with Trump and Putin, on the other hand, could prove largely symbolic. For Xi, “it provides the appearance of China shaping the world order as an equal to the United States,” said Dr Kevork Oskanian, an expert on Russia at the University of Exeter. “Agreement on substantial challenges, which would, in any case, require extensive preparatory negotiations, is unlikely.”.

Recent findings suggest that for China’s ruling Communist party, the political pomp has another key purpose. Nordin stated summits were “occasions for leaders to tell stories about the world, about their country’s place in it … and one of the most key audiences for those stories is at home.”.

For the locals watching the skyscraper light show on Monday night, the symbolism was not lost. China’s export might had helped it become increasingly powerful on the world stage, remarked one local man, who did not give his name. “It’s so great that the summit will take place in Shenzhen,” he said. “I feel very proud.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, model ML, a London-based startup that uses AI to automate work traditionally performed by junior bankers and consultants, including building financial models, preparing pitch decks, and writing due diligence reports, has raised $250 million in Series B funding at a $1.5 billion valuation. The new round, which comes a year after its $75 million Series A round was announced, was co-led by General Atlantic and earlier backer QED Investors.

Brothers Chaz and Arnie Englander co-founded the three-year-old startup after previously co-founding two other companies, including Fat Llama, a peer-to-peer rental marketplace acquired by Swedish rival Hygglo for $41.5 million in 2022.

Sources indicate that model ML develops AI agents that integrate with clients’ systems, data, and tools, including Excel and PowerPoint. The startup indicates its agents understand the full context of deals that bankers and consultants are working on and can automatically patch financial models and presentations when upcoming developments affect their analysis.

Other startups automating the routine, repetitive tasks for investment bankers and management consultants include Hebbia and Rogo, which raised $160 million at a $2 billion valuation in April.

Anthropic and OpenAI have also built tools for financial professionals, but Model ML claims it runs on open source models and that doing so allows it to operate at about 2% of the cost of frontier models while delivering faster results.

NASA's Voyager 1 space probe is now one light-day away from Earth

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (328 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It traveled more than 49 years to get to this point, and its journey isn’t done yet.
  • If NASA's estimates are correct, Voyager 1 is already one light-day away from our planet.
  • "It's never happened before, and it may never happen again — it's that kind of extraordinary," remarked Voyager mission manager Kareem Badaruddin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It traveled more than 49 years to get to this point, and its journey isn’t done yet.

If NASA's estimates are correct, Voyager 1 is already one light-day away from our planet. NASA expects it to have reached that milestone at 5:16:07 AM Eastern time today, November 18. One light-day is the distance a particle of light can travel in a day. Since radio waves travel at the speed of light, it now takes 24 hours to send a command to the probe and 24 hours to get a message back. That's why NASA won't be able to confirm exactly what time it reached one light-day away until tomorrow, when the probe's message arrives.

"It's never happened before, and it may never happen again — it's that kind of extraordinary," remarked Voyager mission manager Kareem Badaruddin.

Industry observers note that voyager 1 headed to space in 1977 as part of NASA's program to study not just our Solar System, but also interstellar space. It was released 16 days after Voyager 2, but it has since traveled farther than its twin and any other probe we've sent out. Voyager 1 reached interstellar space — that's the region between star systems — back in 2012, before Voyager 2 did. It suffered technical glitches, and NASA had to shut down some of its features to keep it going despite the diminishing plutonium in its generator. But it's still around and hasn't stopped its journey.

After traveling for 49 years, two months and 11 days, it's now believed to be about 16 billion miles from our planet—and it's not done yet. Voyager 1 is headed toward a star called Gliese 445, about 17 light-years from Earth in the Ursa Minor constellation. In terms of space distances, that's not so far away. However, none of us would be here by the time it reaches that goal: It's expected to pass within 1.7 light-years of Gliese 445 in 40,000 years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Pakistani man with ties to Iran's government has been sentenced to 27 years in prison for his role in a plot to assassinate US President Donald Trump and other officials.

Asif Merchant was found guilty in March of attempting to commit an act of terrorism transcending national boundaries and murder for hire after trying to hire hitmen to kill Trump, former President Joe Biden, and former US ambassador to the United Nations Nikki Haley.

The hitmen were instead undercover FBI agents.

In court, he remarked he was acting under the direction of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) to avenge the 2020 US assassination of Qasem Soleimani, Iran's topmost military commander.

Latest York US federal judge Eric Ross Komitee sentenced Merchant on Tuesday to 330 months (27 years and six months) in prison, months after a jury handed its guilty verdict.

It has been revealed that although other US officials were potential targets, the assassination plot was largely focused on Trump because he was president at the time Soleimani was killed. Trump has spoken publicly about ordering the US airstrike that killed the Iranian general while he was travelling in Iraq.

In response to the killing, Iran's late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei stated "severe revenge awaits the criminals" behind the attack.

Prosecutors stated Merchant initially travelled to Iran for religious pilgrimages and he was then introduced to an IRGC handler. He travelled to Iran 15 times where he received training from Iranian intelligence officers, prosecutors said, before flying to the US in April 2024 to carry out the plot.

Sources indicate that prosecutors noted Merchant paid $5,000 to the undercover hitmen as part of an initial payment. He was arrested in July 2024 in Texas as he was about to leave the US.

In court, Merchant argued that he "had no other option" than to go along with the plot because his handler indicated that he knew who Merchant's Iranian relatives were and where they lived.

It has been revealed that he mentioned he had anticipated being arrested before anyone was killed and intended to cooperate with the US government, CBS, the BBC's US partner reported. He had hoped that would help him obtain a green card.

The jury deliberated for less than two hours before returning its verdict, US media said.

"An Iranian agent who came to the United States to coordinate an assassination attempt against President Trump has been justly sentenced for his criminal conduct," Attorney General Todd Blanche stated in a statement.

"The Department of Justice will not tolerate foreign terrorist plots against our leaders and will not stop until those responsible are held accountable.".

Additional reporting by Nardine Saad.

#23794. Industry News: How a green economy could help reverse climate change

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1424 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: How a green economy could help reverse climate change

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1424 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that human civilization is presently profoundly unsustainable.
  • If economies and societies keep to business as usual, the Earth's vital processes will continue to be thrown wildly out of balance, threatening the future of humanity.
  • It's now largely accepted that if humans are to have any chance of slowing global warming and nature loss, those social and economic models must change.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that human civilization is presently profoundly unsustainable. Earth has already crossed seven of the nine planetary boundaries critical for sustaining life, including climate change, ocean acidification and biosphere integrity.

If economies and societies keep to business as usual, the Earth's vital processes will continue to be thrown wildly out of balance, threatening the future of humanity.

It's now largely accepted that if humans are to have any chance of slowing global warming and nature loss, those social and economic models must change. That's where the idea of green growth comes in.

Its promise is to keep growing the economy while reducing emissions and resource use. That involves, for instance, running factories, businesses and homes on wind, solar and other green energy instead of coal and gas, replacing gas-fired furnaces with heat pumps and  recycling and reusing resources and raw materials.

Recent findings suggest that "Basically, the idea is: business as usual, but with more sustainable technologies," stated Helmut Haberl, a social ecology professor at BOKU University in Vienna. Along with his colleagues, he published a major report in 2020 evaluating more than 800 studies on green growth.

In principle, the world's economic output could continue to grow in the long term and generate significantly fewer emissions from the burning of fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas. That's been shown in scenarios modeled by researchers with the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, or IPCC.

Thanks to renewable energy and green technologies, those scenarios have already become reality in several countries and regions.

Sources indicate that the economies of developed countries like the United Kingdom, the United States, Japan and Australia have experienced years of growth alongside sinking CO2 emissions. That's even when offshore production is included.

In the European Union, the bloc-wide economy has grown by more than 70% since 1990. Meanwhile, the EU's carbon emissions have dropped by around 40%.

But such a complete decoupling of growth and emissions is, according to Haberl and his fellow researchers, relatively rare.

Recent findings suggest that in India, and in several countries in Africa and Southeast Asia, economies are becoming more efficient. But while economic performance is outpacing emissions growth, emissions are still rising in those countries and globally. This is not compatible with preventing the worst impacts of climate change.

"That doesn't mean, however, that it couldn't work in the future," noted Haberl, referring to decoupling of growth and emissions.

And even though economic growth has been shown to be compatible with emissions reduction, eliminating all greenhouse gases from a polluting industry like steel or chemicals is complicated.

These sectors don't just release emissions by burning fossil fuels for energy; carbon is also a key part of the chemical processes used to create their products, notably in the steel industry.

Replacing it with greener substitutes, or an alternative energy source like green hydrogen, requires significant investment.

Sources indicate that there's another hurdle: the world's high consumption of resources. A productive economy depends on many raw materials and other products: ores, chemicals, wood, cement, glass and agricultural products.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Many countries are now using green technologies to reduce the amount of resources needed to manufacture a product, for example, and are making their economies more efficient.

But that doesn't mean overall fewer resources are being used because falling costs can encourage businesses to produce more things and people to consume more. This can partially offset green savings and is called the rebound effect.

The British economy has been growing for years, emissions have been dropping and efficiency has increased, but the UK still used 7% more resources in 2023 than it did in 2001.

Global resource consumption has tripled over the last 50 years. If the world continues on the current pathway, that could increase by another 60% by 2060. It remains unclear whether green growth can deliver the emissions and resource reductions needed to stop climate change and biodiversity loss rapidly enough.

"We really need to move beyond efficiency gains in our existing production practices to look more broadly at what we consume," noted Catherine Ganzleben, a sustainability and fair transitions expert at the European Environment Agency.

She told DW that people also need to reconsider how they consume and whether they really need to own everything they use in their daily life — cars, for example.

"But we can shift towards models where we share cars, so we pool our resources and have significantly lower resources per person through sharing the goods that we need.".

Some researchers have concluded that unrestricted economic growth is no longer possible in the long term, even if it's sustainable.

Instead, they've called for degrowth. This posits slower economic growth, no growth at all or even negative growth, so that the world's ecosystems and the climate have a chance to recover and stabilize.

That applies mainly to economies in richer countries, which would need to take targeted steps to reduce their energy and resource use. Poorer countries would continue to grow until their economies and quality of life improve significantly.

Under the degrowth theory, a society's prosperity is not measured solely by the growth of its gross domestic product, but by values such as quality of life, education and community. The idea is that once countries develop to a certain point, additional growth doesn't translate into greater well-being.

Sources indicate that ultimately, the concept is based on the idea that human well-being and ecological sustainability is only possible in the long term with a planned, socially just reduction of material production and resource consumption. Degrowth advocates argue this would be preferable to an unplanned and potentially catastrophic economic contraction caused by escalating climate extremes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A 2020 study by researchers from the universities of Leeds and Lausanne demonstrated that the concept of degrowth supported the world's climate goals — and that a high quality of life didn't have to be sacrificed in exchange for a significantly lower consumption of energy and resources.

However, there is still no conclusive evidence that an entire modern economy could continue to function entirely on the degrowth principles in the long term.

Nevertheless, Haberl doesn't assume that an environmentally friendly economic model automatically goes hand in hand with sacrifice, arguing instead for a needs-based economy.

It has been revealed that "A society isn't necessarily better off when it's producing more goods and services," he mentioned. It all depends on how prosperity and quality of life are measured in the future, and how states decide to do business.

According to recent reports, today, a successful economy is measured by the growth of a country's gross domestic product — put simply, the worth of all of its goods and services. This calculation doesn't account for income distribution, unpaid work, quality of life or environmental damage.

Industry observers note that "The highest possible real incomes for every individual would probably not be compatible with ecological goals in the long term," stated Haberl. "On the other hand, an increase in prosperity — related to a higher quality of life — would be.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

An analysis by the European Environment Agency (EEA) pointed out that the idea of steady growth is part of the world's economic cycle, and deeply anchored in our institutions, norms and societal discourse. The job market and tax system are also closely tied to gross domestic product growth. A shrinking economy would therefore require a fundamental shift in our way of thinking.

Countries face a dilemma: a steadily growing economy is not compatible with ecological goals, according to the EEA. On the other side, a sharp decline in growth could trigger enormous social upheaval.

And the correlation is much more complex than the idea of "less is more," as highlighted by an EEA study in November 2021. "The fact that GDP growth has been harmful for the environment does not necessarily mean that declining GDP would be good for the environment," noted the report.

Achieving green growth while respecting environmental limits would require an "unprecedented decoupling of economic activity from environmental and climate pressures. Whether this is feasible is currently uncertain.".

This article was originally written in German.

San Diego dumps both Flock cameras and smart streetlights

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (615 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Monday evening, San Diego’s city council voted to end its contracts with two surveillance equipment vendors, Flock and Ubicquia.
  • “We fucking won!” said Lilly Irani of the Transparent and Responsible Use of Surveillance Technology (TRUST) SD Coalition, speaking in her personal capacity.
  • She and her colleagues have been among the loudest critics in recent years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Monday evening, San Diego’s city council voted to end its contracts with two surveillance equipment vendors, Flock and Ubicquia. San Diego is one of the largest cities to end its relationship with Flock, the startup with an estimated valuation of $8.3 billion.

“We fucking won!” said Lilly Irani of the Transparent and Responsible Use of Surveillance Technology (TRUST) SD Coalition, speaking in her personal capacity.

She and her colleagues have been among the loudest critics in recent years.

“The national energy creating left and right and center coalitions was the major cause [of the political victory],” she remarked, noting that it was only last month that one of the council members revoked his support, creating an opening for a political majority to halt the surveillance.

That council member, Stephen Whitburn, said in an October press conference that he wanted his fellow citizens to “feel safe.”.

“If Flock cameras are causing many San Diegans to feel unsafe, then they have lost effectiveness as a public safety tool,” he noted at the time.

After the Monday vote, San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria mentioned in a social media post that he “respect[ed] the Council’s decision” and would not veto the move to stop operation of the cameras across the city.

Sources indicate that andrew Smith, a spokesperson for Flock, told Ars in an email on Tuesday that the organization also “respect[s] the city’s decision.” But Flock isn’t happy about it. “When a tool that is actively helping solve violent crimes is removed, public safety moves backward,” Smith wrote. “That has real consequences: cases will take longer to solve, organized retail theft crews will operate with fewer obstacles, a missing child may not be returned home, and victims may wait longer, or indefinitely, for justice.”.

At Monday’s city council meeting, police representatives said there has been a 20 percent decline in vehicle theft since 2023, with 689 stolen vehicles recovered as a result of the Flock cameras.

The vote is a remarkable turnabout from just three years ago, when the mayor and other municipal leaders urged the city council to approve the program.

According to recent reports, the city’s wholesale rejection of these devices included Ubicquia’s so-called “smart streetlights” that worked in concert with Flock’s AI-driven automatic license plate reader (ALPR) software. This cessation of smart streetlights marks the second time in less than a decade that San Diego has experimented with and then ultimately rejected this technology.

At one point, San Diego purchased thousands of smart streetlight systems from a different vendor, GE Current, but a previous mayoral administration shuttered them in 2020. After that, Ubicquia acquired the smart city platform and proposed a newer installation of 500 cameras in 2023 in partnership with Flock—and supported by police—which was installed in 2023.

Industry observers note that at the time, a local watchdog agency, the City of San Diego Privacy Advisory Board, asked the city council to vote down the initiative. One of its board members, Pegah Parsi, wrote on LinkedIn that she is now feeling “vindication.”.

Industry observers note that “A reminder for every city, agency, and institution: if you create an advisory board of experts, listen to them!” she wrote. “Actually, earnestly listen to them. It’s cheaper than learning the hard way. Do better.”.

That sentiment is echoed by Secure Justice, an Oakland-based advocacy group, which has been studying and monitoring Flock’s problems nationwide.

“We’ve documented at least 513 Flock contracts that have ended in red and blue states, in large and small cities,” Brian Hofer, the group’s executive director, emailed Ars. “It’s pretty clear that Americans do not consent to their government tracking them as we go about our daily lives.”.

Sony might be attempting to patch jailbreak vulnerabilities before the biggest game of the year launches.

Grand Theft Auto VI fans will have to download a new PlayStation 5 update, or they won't be able to launch the game. Sony has released new firmware for the console that's required to access the long-awaited title. It's encouraging fans on X to download and install it before the game's release at midnight on November 19, so they don't have to wait a second longer to start playing.

In a recent development, as IGN reports, PS5 firmware revision 14.23 is 1.267GB in size and contains "security fixes to the system software." Sony didn't say why it's required to run GTA VI on the PS5. Sources indicate that those planning to get the game sometime today may want to purchase and install it soon. The digital version is 212GB in size and would take more than an hour to download for those with a 1Gbps internet connection. Rockstar Games has also rolled out pre-release patches since GTA VI became available for pre-order, with the latest one being 600 MB. The patches should automatically download for those who've already preloaded the game.

Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software enhancement that is required before playing Grand Theft Auto VI. Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19 so that they're ready to play on launch day, November 19.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Waymo robotaxis are no longer allowed to operate on California freeways after the state’s Department of Motor Vehicles restricted the Alphabet-owned organization’s operations following several incidents that raised safety concerns.

California’s DMV, which regulates the testing and deployment of autonomous vehicles in the state, issued the operational restrictions on Waymo on November 11. However, the restrictions weren’t made public until Tuesday. San Francisco Business Times was the first to report the order.

The DMV confirmed the new restrictions to TechCrunch, stating that the department took action after three Waymo autonomous vehicles entered an active construction closure on U.S. Route 101 near Burlingame, and another separate incident involving California Highway Patrol vehicles on Highway 280 in San Francisco.

Recent findings suggest that waymo has complied and is preventing its robotaxis from accessing freeways in any of the markets it operates in, including those outside of California. Waymo currently has commercial operations in 15 U.S. cities.

The DMV stated Waymo’s freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety.

“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present, despite a prior restriction and corrective actions implemented following similar incidents that occurred on May 18, 2026,” according to an emailed statement sent to TechCrunch.

The DMV said the restrictions will remain in place until Waymo can demonstrate that it has taken “effective corrective actions” to address the deficiencies.

Waymo spokesperson Dana Gallagher told TechCrunch the company has temporarily restricted freeway operations across its other operating markets to evaluate its performance.

“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do,” Gallagher remarked in a statement. “Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”.

Waymo began offering freeway rides in late 2025, a commercial milestone that has been central to its expansion in major metro areas. Freeway access allows Waymo to connect riders to airports and other destinations more efficiently, slashing travel times by avoiding slower surface streets.

According to recent reports, that has been particularly important in the San Francisco Bay Area because Waymo’s service area stretches from the city south to Silicon Valley. Freeway access has dramatically shortened trips across the Peninsula that previously took 45 minutes or more than an hour.

In May, Waymo abruptly stopped operating on highways. The manufacturer didn’t cite a specific reason at the time, but several social media posts revealed Waymo robotaxis driving through traffic cones and struggling to navigate construction zones.

Waymo robotaxis returned to freeways in July after the firm stated it updated the self-driving software system to improve performance around freeway construction zones.
