📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Waymo has temporarily suspended its driverless vehicles from operating on all US freeways, the tech giant has said.

The decision comes after California banned Waymo's driverless taxis from state freeways following a series of recent traffic incidents.

California's Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) cited an "imminent hazard to public safety" for the ban, noting an incident this month in which several driverless Waymo vehicles entered an active construction zone on US Route 101.

Waymo said it was working with state officials "diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations", adding that no injuries or collisions were reported following the incident on US Route 101 south of San Francisco.

California's DMV said Waymo's driverless taxis presented a risk "due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present".

In another incident earlier this month, footage widely seen on social media appeared to show a Waymo car trying to overtake patrol vehicles that were deliberately slowing the pace of traffic on a San Francisco highway.

The California ban, which came into effect on 11 November, would remain in place until Waymo "demonstrates to the department that it has taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions".

A Waymo spokesperson remarked: "In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance.".

Data on Waymo's website suggests that its cars, compared to human drivers, are involved in 95% fewer crashes resulting in serious injury.

Waymo at the moment operates driverless taxis in 15 US cities, but only offered freeway rides in a handful of those locations, including San Francisco, Los Angeles and Miami.

The company's driverless taxis can continue to operate on regular city streets.

In May, Waymo recalled thousands of its self-driving cars in the US over a software concern that could allow vehicles to drive into flooded roads.

In the same month, multiple Waymo cars were spotted driving around a cul-de-sac in Atlanta, Georgia, in the early hours of the morning.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The integrity of South Korea’s career-defining university entrance exam has been thrown into doubt after the top scorer in a recent professional exam admitted using a concealed camera and AI to cheat.
  • On Thursday, more than half a million people, mostly school students, are due to sit the exam, known as the suneung, at 1,312 centres across the country.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

South Korea has been gripped by revelations of AI-aided cheating, just days before more than half a million students are to sit high-stakes entrance exams.

The integrity of South Korea’s career-defining university entrance exam has been thrown into doubt after the top scorer in a recent professional exam admitted using a concealed camera and AI to cheat.

On Thursday, more than half a million people, mostly school students, are due to sit the exam, known as the suneung, at 1,312 centres across the country. The exam runs for a gruelling eight hours over a single day and determines which university a candidate can attend and, in turn, their future prospects.

Recent findings suggest that the country goes to great lengths to ensure the smooth running of the suneung. Aircraft take-offs and landings are rescheduled during the 25-minute English listening paper to minimise noise, while artillery fire and tank movements are suspended.

The stock market opens an hour late and cars are stopped 200 metres from every centre. Extra trains run from 6am, police drive latecomers to their exam halls, and tourist attractions open late to ease traffic. Offices are asked to open at 10am.

But in recent days, exam organisers have faced a renewed threat to the validity of the entire exercise, after the top scorer in this year’s tax accountancy exam- who got just one question wrong out of 160– admitted on Sunday he had cheated by using AI.

Prime minister Han Seong-sook told a cabinet meeting in Seoul on Tuesday that AI-assisted cheating was a “social evil” that the government would “root out”.

“We will block outright the carrying of smart devices during the exam,” she said. The education ministry and other agencies should approach it “as if staking their jobs on it”, she added.

Han noted smart devices must be turned off and handed in, while bags left in corridors would be checked for any devices that were still on. Exam officials would also inspect all candidates’ glasses and watches, as well as their collars, sleeves and buttons for concealed cameras.

The government will also send emergency alerts to every phone in the country, which sound at full volume and cannot be silenced, in the hope of catching out anyone who has not handed in their device.

More invigilators will be deployed, and the government stated it was preparing to switch off school wifi inside exam centres and public wifi nearby, and that personal hotspots, which cannot be blocked, would be traced through connection records.

The weekend’s cheating revelation captured national headlines in South Korea, stoking concern about the security of the suneung.

It has been revealed that in a video posted to his lawyer’s YouTube channel, the exam cheat noted he had photographed the questions with a concealed microcamera, sent them to an AI system and read the answers from a smartphone. “I cheated in the tax accountant exam,” he said. “My top placing is not the result of legitimate effort.”.

According to recent reports, his lawyer handed police a camera, a laptop and a phone. No charges have been brought, and the prime minister has ordered procedures to begin that would void his result and bar him for five years.

The education minister, Choi Kyo-jin, told parliament on Monday that while authorities could screen out the smart glasses already on sale at Thursday’s exam, newer variants could not be dealt with perfectly.

Choi has ruled out postponing the exam, which has been delayed several times before, including in 2017, after an earthquake struck the south-eastern city of Pohang, and in 2020 due to the Covid pandemic.

Sources indicate that smart glasses have been banned in exams since the end of June. In October, several candidates were caught with them while sitting university-run admissions exams. At the suneung, wearing a pair counts as using one even when switched off.

The education ministry looked at using radio-frequency equipment to detect the glasses in exam halls, but concluded conditions varied too much between venues for deployment this year. Checks will instead rely on visual inspection, with at least one dedicated official placed in each exam centre.

Teachers’ unions have criticised the government response as belated. A survey last month of 2,716 secondary school teachers by the Korean Teachers and Education Workers Union demonstrated that 82.3% said they could not tell whether a candidate was wearing smart glasses under the current procedure, with only 3.5% saying they could.

To avoid facing scrutiny on exam day, some candidates are reportedly switching to contact lenses. An optician in Suwon, south of Seoul, noted students who had never worn contacts were coming in to ask how to put them in.

Han said on X on Monday that the checks would be handled carefully “so that candidates acting in good faith do not suffer unnecessary anxiety or inconvenience”.

It has been revealed that in his video confession, the accountancy test cheat addressed suneung candidates directly. “The suneung is coming up soon,” he noted.

“To anyone thinking of cheating as I did: I am going to tell the investigators everything, so please don’t think, ‘I won’t get caught.’”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, was Google feeling a little left out of the recent wave of tech outages?
  • As it turns out, the company was trying to head off reports of a Gmail outage that began circulating on X on Tuesday around the same time that Apple was seeing a number of verified outages of its own.
  • Industry observers note that the concerns seemed to stem from an X post by Downdetector, a crowdsourced website where owners can report service disruptions themselves and see if others are having problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, was Google feeling a little left out of the recent wave of tech outages? The company took to X on Tuesday to announce that its Gmail service is actually running just fine. In a post, the company stated it was not currently seeing evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption and reminded owners they could always check Gmail’s real-time status on its online dashboard.

As it turns out, the company was trying to head off reports of a Gmail outage that began circulating on X on Tuesday around the same time that Apple was seeing a number of verified outages of its own. While some posts on the social network suggested Gmail was experiencing a disruption, others mentioned they were not having any problems.

Industry observers note that the concerns seemed to stem from an X post by Downdetector, a crowdsourced website where owners can report service disruptions themselves and see if others are having problems. Downdetector is not an official source for verifying or understanding the true scope of internet outages, and as people become more concerned about possible cyberattacks, the site’s data may become less valuable over time if every minor glitch and hiccup is reported as an “outage” by non-technical users.

According to recent reports, the fact that Google had to announce it was not having an outage speaks to the growing anxiety around the reliability of major tech services. Over the past week, Apple and Microsoft experienced outages, an FAA network failure led to a nationwide ground stop, and some banks and airlines also reported disruptions.

Industry observers note that however, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton stated on Fox Business Network’s “The Claman Countdown” on Tuesday that the U.S. is not right now facing coordinated cyberattacks. He told the outlet, “We do not see the indicia of a coordinated cyberattack — let me just be clear about that — and we do not see the indicia of state-sponsored activity here.”.

Industry observers note that instead, Clayton attributed the rise in issues to businesses patching their systems. The patching may be a downstream effect of AI, as newer models have become increasingly adept at uncovering previously unknown vulnerabilities. “They’re upgrading them, they’re putting patches in place,” he said, adding that this is happening at “a much larger scale” than before.

As a result, some of the systems are “not coming back as expected in all cases,” he added.

APEC summit: Xi, Trump and Putin gather in Shenzhen, China

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Here are the biggest headlines from Trump's Asia tour on Wednesday, November 18:.
  • Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum won praise on Chinese social media for her frugal travel prepares this week, taking an economy flight to Shenzhen.
  • The Mexican president took a South China Airlines flight from Mexico City to Shenzhen, with posts going viral on China's Weibo social media site seemingly showing Sheinbaum chatting with other passengers on board.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here are the biggest headlines from Trump's Asia tour on Wednesday, November 18:.

Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum won praise on Chinese social media for her frugal travel prepares this week, taking an economy flight to Shenzhen.

The Mexican president took a South China Airlines flight from Mexico City to Shenzhen, with posts going viral on China's Weibo social media site seemingly showing Sheinbaum chatting with other passengers on board.

She posted a short video on social media showing her being greeted by Chinese officials and schoolchildren after getting off an airport bus, as well as an earlier post showing her waiting in Mexico City's airport departures lounge.

A hashtag on Weibo about her arrival attracted more than 10 million views, with users voicing admiration for her low-cost intercontinental travel.

"It's commendable to spend taxpayer money frugally and ensure it's used where it's most needed, rather than squandering it on luxurious private jets or official travel expenses," the AFP news agency cited one user as saying.

Sheinbaum is promoting an austerity program debuted by her predecessor, Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador, who put the Mexican presidential plane up for sale in 2023.

She traveled with a large delegation of ministers to Shenzhen.

China has become particularly sensitive to the idea of corruption and wasteful public spending in recent years amid high-profile and long-running anti-corruption measures launched by President Xi Jinping, seemingly at least partly as damage-limitation efforts following a series of scandals.

The leaders of Canada and Mexico have both reported on separate meetings with the US president on the sidelines of the APEC summit, amid difficult trade talks with the main economic power in the Americas.

"The leaders discussed the work underway to reach a mutually beneficial trade agreement that would create jobs, boost affordability, and fully respect Canada's languages, culture, and sovereignty," Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's office said. "They agreed to continue the work and to stay in close contact.".

Meanwhile, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum published a photo of her "very good meeting with President Donald Trump and his team" online, saying "we continue to make progress on our shared agenda.".

The presidents of the US and Russia have shaken hands in their first in-person meeting since August 2025, when Putin was invited to Alaska for talks primarily concerning Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin shook hands in the presence of host Xi Jinping ahead of the leaders' welcome banquet at the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

The encounter follows a rare sign of progress in the US-led efforts to broker an end to the war between Russia and Ukraine, a conflict Trump repeatedly claimed he would settle in "a day" if reelected.

The two are expected to have a private meeting on Thursday.

Talks took place last week in Abu Dhabi involving Russia, Ukraine and European representatives, with Trump's negotiating team subsequently traveling to the Kremlin for a meeting with Putin and other Russian officials.

Trump's arrival was highly choreographed: He descended from Air Force One and stood on a red carpet lined with people waving colorful pom poms. Trump and Xi hugged before shaking hands.

The White House, other countries and Donald Trump himself have all listed possible or probable bilateral or multilateral talks involving the US president on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, beyond Thursday's highly-anticipated US-China-Russia meeting.

Some of the more notable examples are listed here:.

Chinese news agency Xinhua has reported the first comments from Xi Jinping to Donald Trump following his arrival.

"I look forward to an in-depth exchange of views with you on major concerns concerning China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape," Xi told Trump.

He stated the talks would take place "with the aim of advancing a constructive, strategically stable relationship between our two nations — one built upon the foundations of mutual respect, fairness and reciprocity.".

Despite Trump and Xi's efforts to regularly hold friendly face-to-face talks in recent months, the US and China are nevertheless embroiled in difficult trade negotiations as the two superpowers try to reconcile competing interests on various concerns.

The two sides have been periodically extending a temporary tariff truce designed to bridge the gap until they can reach a more permanent agreement, which for now has proven elusive. China announced the most recent extension earlier this month, to run until early January.

The interim CEO of US chip giant Nvidia says the manufacturer is not currently shipping Hopper-generation data center products to China.

These are some of the most advanced Nvidia products licensed for export by the US government; the firm had sold such goods worth $2.4 billion (roughly €2.2 billion) in the previous quarter, Colette Kress said.

Kress replaced Jensen Huang following his resignation last week and amid the scandal over alleged Chinese attempts both to gain intelligence on the manufacturer's CEO and to circumvent import restrictions.

"Our guidance does not have any licensed Hopper data center products included, and we are no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China," Kress said.

She did not specify why such deliveries had currently stopped or say whether the step would be permanent.

Huang was influential in persuading Donald Trump to allow sales of H200 Hopper processors used to train and run advanced AI models to China, reversing export controls the US had imposed in 2022 under Trump's predecessor Joe Biden.

China has called the allegations of espionage targeting Nvidia unfounded and threatened to respond in kind if restrictions on trade follow as a result of the fallout from Huang's resignation.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US President Donald Trump has landed at Shenzhen Airport on Air Force One and disembarked.

He left Manila in the Philippines a few hours earlier.

Trump will be attending the APEC summit but is also expected to take part in a three-way meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday.

Xi greeted Trump at the airport on Wednesday, mirroring a gesture Trump had recently extended during the Chinese leader's state visit to the US in September.

Sanae Takaichi arrived in China for the APEC summit, which is also her first official visit to the country as Japanese prime minister.

Takaichi's moves to bolster Japan's military and comments last year on Taiwan have upset Beijing and severely affected bilateral ties.

In particular, Takaichi's suggestion that Tokyo could intervene militarily if Beijing sought to forcibly take Taiwan — which China considers its territory — led to friction between the regional rivals with a troubled 20th century history and ongoing territorial disputes.

China imposed trade restrictions and urged citizens not to travel to Japan, which had become an increasingly popular tourist destination. Traffic is down by roughly half this year as a result.

A formal one-on-one meeting between Takaichi and China's Xi Jinping is considered highly unlikely, but Japan's NHK public broadcaster did report that Xi would "personally greet her" before Wednesday's banquet.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The leaders of China, the United States and Russia are due to hold their first trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit this week.

Separately, US President Donald Trump will also hold talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping during the November 18-19 gathering in Shenzhen, China.

With different priorities on trade, Ukraine, Iran and arms control, what does each leader hope to gain?

Read DW's full report on what Trump, Xi and Putin are hoping to extract from the trilateral talks.

Canada and China are moving to give each other's financial firms greater access to their markets, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney mentioned during a speech at the APEC summit.

"When our businesses depend on ​too few currencies or single payment channels, disruption, when it comes, can spread rapidly," ​he noted, adding that China and Canada had renewed the ​currency swap arrangement ‌between their central banks and were issuing each other's currencies.

Carney's comments came a day after he and President Xi held talks in Shenzhen to produce deals to further reduce tariffs. Ottawa is re-engaging with China after years of strained relations as it looks to reduce its reliance on the US.

Industry observers note that president Trump on Wednesday mentioned that the US has just concluded a "very major trade deal" with the Philippines, albeit without providing details. Manila has not yet confirmed any agreement.

"We've just consummated a very significant trade deal, the ​biggest trade deal we've ever made so far, and it ​is a fair deal for both countries," Trump ​mentioned during ‌a state luncheon at the Philippine presidential palace.

"We were very happy with that, and we didn't know ‌that was going to take place, but it took ‌place ​very rapidly and it's a magnificent deal for both," he noted.

Trade negotiations were not listed in the schedules provided by Washington or Manila.

The Philippines' ambassador to the US, Jose Manuel Romualdez ​said, "The US offered ‌for us to diversify our food supply and energy requirements.".

However, Romualdez told Reuters that nothing had been signed.

The two-day APEC summit has kicked off in China's southern city of Shenzhen. DW's Rik Glauert in Taipei offers a preview of what host, Xi Jinping, is hoping to achieve.

President Xi pledged to stand against trade protectionism in his speech at the APEC summit on Wednesday, in a subtle slight towards the United States and the trade war waged by its president.

Xi urged support for what he called "free and open trade," trying to ​portray his country as a stable partner on the global stage in contrast with its main economic rival, the US, which has raised tariffs ‌under President Trump.

His remarks came after Washington revealed further restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips from companies such as Nvidia, further complicating a trade truce between the two superpowers.

Xi urged that China and Russia, together, take concrete measures to further cooperation and "lead and advance the ⁠trend toward ​a multipolar world.".

Chinese and Russian news agencies reported at around noon on Wednesday that Xi and Putin had met for talks. That's the fifth time the two leaders have met this year, including once by video link.

Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday said he expected major benefits from his upcoming trilateral meet with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Speaking at the opening ceremony of the APEC summit, Putin called for partnership over isolation, citing a fragmented global economy and military-political risks.

"I therefore expect big potential benefit ​from the ‌upcoming trilateral meeting between the leaders of Russia, China and ​the United ⁠States, which is scheduled to take place ⁠on ​the sidelines of the APEC summit," Putin told the summit.

The Russian leader held bilateral talks with Xi ahead of the pair's trilateral talks with Trump on Thursday.

Putin said Chinese and Russian foreign policy was working "steadily and positively on the international stage.".

A British hacker has been sentenced to six years in a federal prison in the US for conspiring to hack into at least a dozen companies via text message phishing, and stealing more than $11.6m (Â£8.8m) in cryptocurrency from individual victims.

Tyler Buchanan, 24, from Dundee, started hacking as a teenager and was part of the collective of young hackers known as Scattered Spider, which has been blamed for a string of high profile cyber-crimes.

US prosecutors remarked the thefts had "severe, life-altering consequences" for victims and showed the growing threat posed by online crime groups.

The sentence brings to an end a years-long international investigation involving authorities in the UK, US, Spain and Canada.

Buchanan admitted taking part in a hacking campaign that began in 2021, when he was 19.

Working from his parents' home, he and other English-speaking hackers in the US and UK targeted employees at major technology and telecommunications companies.

It made them $8m in less than two years, according to US prosecutors.

Buchanan and his hacker gang sent out hundreds of SMS messages to the mobile phones of people who worked for large tech or telecoms companies.

The SMS phishing messages contained links to spoof websites designed to look like legitimate sites of victim companies.

The websites then lured the recipient into providing confidential information, including personal identifying information (PII), and account usernames and passwords.

The boys and young men did it on an industrial scale with Buchanan setting up a Telegram bot to collect all the victims' credentials as the duped workers unwittingly handed over their login details.

For some victim companies, subsequently stolen information included confidential work information, intellectual property, plus account access credentials, names, email addresses, and telephone numbers.

The group then used stolen information and SIM-swapping techniques to target cryptocurrency investors in the United States.

In the largest single theft, prosecutors said one victim lost $1.67m in December 2022.

Overall, authorities calculated that Buchanan and his co-conspirators stole more than $11.6m from victims.

Buchanan was also a victim of cyber-criminals.

In early 2023 his online identity and home address were leaked by rival hackers seeking access to his cryptocurrency.

Cyber security researchers and journalists reported that he was assaulted at his home and threatened with a blowtorch.

"TylerB and his group were highly sophisticated and organised but the violence he and others experienced was a sign of the troubling direction of these online communities of young hackers" says cyber security researcher Allison Nixon from Unit221B.

Buchanan then reportedly fled to Canada to escape further threats before returning home.

In April 2023, officers from Police Scotland searched Buchanan's bedroom after receiving a request from the FBI.

Investigators recovered a device containing the names and addresses of hacking victims, along with cryptocurrency seed phrases and account credentials belonging to at least one victim.

The following month, Buchanan left the UK again.

He was arrested on 31 May 2024 at Palma de Mallorca Airport in Spain while attempting to board a private flight to Naples.

After being extradited to the United States, he remained in custody before being sentenced this week.

In his November 2023 charge, Buchanan was named along with four American men and boys in their twenties and teens for alleged activity linked to the notorious cyber-criminal collective Scattered Spider.

They have all pleaded guilty too and are now serving time in jail.

Two other members of the Scattered Spider group were jailed in the UK in July for various cyber attacks including a disruptive one against Transport for London that caused Â£39m of damage.

Copilot is "the latest OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1109 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the tech giant’s vision for its new “frontier ecosystem,” announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as “the new OS for work.”.
  • In a recent development, the announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software.
  • The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the firm first announced in September.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the tech giant’s vision for its new “frontier ecosystem,” announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as “the new OS for work.”.

In a recent development, the announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the upcoming Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent’s work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. People will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications.

The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the firm first announced in September. Parts of that vision are now becoming “generally available,” as Nadella puts it, with autonomous agents and upcoming governance tools arriving alongside them.

It has been revealed that copilot Autopilot (not to be confused with Windows Autopilot) is a “persistent, proactive agent for personal productivity” according to Microsoft. In a nutshell, Autopilot is a cloud-based autonomous AI agent that customers can delegate responsibilities to, not just single tasks. Autopilot can be authorized to work across services like email and calendars and complete tasks assigned to it as part of its role. Autopilot will use usage-based billing via Copilot Credits, but final pricing has not been announced ahead of general availability.

Industry observers note that also unveiled as generally available at the keynote speech was Microsoft IQ, an intelligence platform that houses Work IQ, a context layer that helps agents understand a company’s communications, relationships, and ongoing work. Nadella described Work IQ as perhaps a company’s most valuable database: “It has a deep understanding of the people, their relationships to other people, your emails, your meetings, chats, projects that make up all the fabric of work.” Whether companies want autonomous agents to have access to internal documents and messaging data will have to be determined by their own internal IT review.

Recent findings suggest that copilot Workspaces is a collaborative environment currently available through Microsoft’s Frontier early-access program, but coming soon will be the ability to bring personal Autopilot agents into Workspaces. Early in the keynote address, Nadella said that “until now, AI interactions have mostly been single-player. Workspaces makes it a truly multiplayer experience, where people and agents drive towards a common goal, with shared context.”.

According to recent reports, trust, the third pillar of Microsoft’s latest frontier ecosystem, was something that Nadella continued returning to during his presentation, and not in a way that some might expect. “We find ourselves in a place where alignment is elusive. Mechanistic understanding of these models is elusive. The question is: How can you even trust all this powerful technology? The reality is, by definition, you can’t,” he said.

In a departure from the norms of “AI is magic” corporate hype sentiment, Nadella conceded that the internal workings of AI thought processes remain difficult to understand, and models cannot be trusted to govern themselves, regardless of whether their answers are accurate. Nadella described the solution as “an architectural imperative to separate the supply of intelligence” from the authority granted to it. Microsoft says each Autopilot agent will have a unique ID, and administrators can restrict permissions or block it entirely. All agent activities are logged for human review, and Autopilot can ask for human approval before engaging in certain actions.

Recent findings suggest that the promised agent controls and admission that AI systems can’t always be trusted are meaningful, but Microsoft is asking businesses and people to place their trust in the company’s own safeguards instead, though the effectiveness of those safeguards against mistakes, rogue actions, or data exposure must still be demonstrated. In Microsoft’s view, the solution to untrustworthy intelligence is not to make AI agents trustworthy, but to control what they’re permitted to do. Businesses will need to decide how much autonomy they delegate to agents.

Along with the guardrails, Microsoft declared what it calls the “AI Transparency Initiative.” The effort has partnered with 40-plus major companies, including Adobe and MasterCard, to develop open, industry-wide standards for AI governance and security. Nadella described the initiative as a way for industry to “help establish an open standard that makes AI safer, more transparent, and more accessible.”.

Along with the other announced additions, Microsoft also announced expanding capabilities for Agent 365, its existing control plane for managing AI agents across enterprise environments. The newly introduced agent sheriff extends existing identity, security, and management systems to AI agents. Microsoft describes the objective as providing “observability at every layer of the stack.” Agent 365 offers governance controls over agent behavior in what Microsoft indicates is “autonomous in execution, but bounded and supervised.”.

Sources indicate that along with Agent 365 comes Agent 365 Business Analytics: “You can simply think of this as an ERP system of AI usage. You can see exactly what’s driving the spend and connect the spend to the outcomes that drive business value,” mentioned Nadella. Customers will be able to see real-world costs associated with AI token-spend and compare those metrics to the value of work performed. Microsoft acknowledged that the estimations of assisted work hours are determined by a model, and not a direct measurement of time that may have been saved. This is a telling concession for Microsoft to make as businesses evaluate whether there will be an ROI on AI implementations, but according to Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft Commercial Business, “anything you can do with Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot, for less.”.

According to recent reports, nadella offered only a brief acknowledgment of last week’s outage that disrupted access to services like Exchange Online and Teams for people across the globe. “Last week was a reminder of how critical digital infrastructure is as the dial tone for the world,” he stated. “We know the trust you place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously, and in that context I know we have work to do.”.

That statement was all the time the elephant in the room was given, but Microsoft did seem to acknowledge the public’s growing concern over data center projects by highlighting the previously discussed “community-first AI infrastructure initiative.” Not a surprise in a presentation that asks organizations to extend more autonomy to software agents, at a time when Microsoft’s existing infrastructure is under increased scrutiny.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mary Peltola defeated the state's Republican incumbent after a controversial race.
  • Democrat Mary Peltola has won Alaska's hard-fought Senate race, completing a sweeping victory for the party in the US upper house in the midterm elections.
  • The win gives the Democrats a 56th Senate seat following a tumultuous and controversial election in Alaska, which featured alleged spoiler recruitment efforts and unprecedented court battles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mary Peltola defeated the state's Republican incumbent after a controversial race.

Democrat Mary Peltola has won Alaska's hard-fought Senate race, completing a sweeping victory for the party in the US upper house in the midterm elections.

The win gives the Democrats a 56th Senate seat following a tumultuous and controversial election in Alaska, which featured alleged spoiler recruitment efforts and unprecedented court battles.

It took two full weeks of counting to call a winner in the 3 November poll due to the logistical challenge of collecting ballots from across the state's remote expanse.

It is the ninth Senate seat the Democrats have taken from Republicans in the midterms, giving the party control of the US Congress for the last two years of Donald Trump's presidency.

The Democrats also won back the House of Representatives, the lower chamber.

Peltola defeated the incumbent Republican senator, Dan S Sullivan, who is yet to comment.

In her victory statement, Peltola said the "status quo in DC is not working for Alaska".

She recalled speaking to "elders in tears about empty fish racks" and to parents in rural Alaska choosing between heating their homes and putting food on the table.

Peltola is the first Alaska Native elected to the US Senate, and is the first Democrat to win a US Senate seat in Alaska since 2008.

Donald Trump won the state by 13 points in the 2024 presidential election, but defeat for the Republicans in this year's US Senate race in the state caps off a string of losses in the midterms for the president's party.

Many voters across the United States cited cost-of-living problems as a factor that affected how they cast their ballots.

It has been revealed that trump notes Alaska voters chose the wrong Dan Sullivan. What does the data show?

Could Alaska's fishing industry tilt Washington's balance of power?

Peltola's campaign had come under fire after the Fresh York Times, external reported that her team worked with people who tried to recruit so-called spoiler candidates in an alleged attempt to confuse voters.

The alleged scheme led to a candidate named Daniel J Sullivan - a complete political unknown residing in a small coastal town who shared a name with the state's current US Senator and incumbent, Dan S Sullivan - contesting the race.

After legal challenges, state courts ruled that Daniel J Sullivan could remain on the ballot, and election officials distinguished them on election materials.

Peltola denied having knowledge of the alleged plot but her campaign swiftly came under fire, and both the US justice department and Alaska's Republican governor noted they would launch investigations.

The Trump administration also filed a lawsuit attempting to stop the certification of the election results if the incumbent Republican Senator Sullivan lost.

A federal judge, though, dismissed the case, following legal challenges from Alaska election officials as well as the Peltola campaign and voting groups.

Due to Alaska's ranked-choice voting system, voters confused about which Dan Sullivan was the incumbent could have simply chosen both men, listing them as their first and second choices.

If they did so, after the first round of voting was complete, tabulation would have re-allocated any votes from Daniel J Sullivan - who stood little to no chance of winning - to Dan S Sullivan.

Experts told the BBC that this process made it difficult for any potential spoiler candidate to have any impact on the results.

An analysis by BBC Verify found that even if every vote for Daniel J Sullivan had gone to the incumbent, Dan S Sullivan, Peltola would still have won.

The Democratic win in Alaska cements the party's majority in the US Senate, as the party now has 56 seats to the Republicans' 44.

According to recent reports, the most senior Democrat in the Senate, Chuck Schumer, said Peltola had run "a pitch-perfect campaign devoted to the problems Alaskans care most about". Hailing the Democrats' final tally in the Senate, he said: "56 seats was an unimaginable result even just a few months ago.".

The Alaska seat was initially one of several toss-up races that appeared as a must-win for Democrats if they wanted to gain control of the US Senate. But by the time Peltola was called the winner, they had seats to spare.

With 99% of ballots counted, Peltola had slightly more than 50% of the votes, while Sullivan trailed on less than 46%.

Sullivan, a former Alaska attorney general and an ally of Trump, campaigned on his record of delivering energy and military investment for the state.

Peltola promised Alaskans a more independent voice in Washington.

"As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first," she stated in her victory statement.

"I will stand up to anyone to take on the rigged system in DC and deliver results for Alaska's working families.".

#23767. Latin America's mega-prisons: Can El Salvador's model work?

Latin America's mega-prisons: Can El Salvador's model work?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (930 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, around 15,000 inmates and a capacity of up to 40,000, prison sentences of up to 1,000 years, strict security measures and an extreme isolation regime.
  • These are just some of the facts circulating about El Salvador's Terrorism Confinement Center (CECOT), a symbol of President Nayib Bukele's security policy and a possible model for other Latin American countries seeking to combat organized crime.
  • More than a dozen governments in the region have proposed building similar "mega-prisons," although most would have a far smaller capacity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, around 15,000 inmates and a capacity of up to 40,000, prison sentences of up to 1,000 years, strict security measures and an extreme isolation regime. Staged images show inmates with shaved heads and tattoos being subdued by heavily armed guards.

These are just some of the facts circulating about El Salvador's Terrorism Confinement Center (CECOT), a symbol of President Nayib Bukele's security policy and a possible model for other Latin American countries seeking to combat organized crime.

More than a dozen governments in the region have proposed building similar "mega-prisons," although most would have a far smaller capacity. A range of experts consulted by DW question the effectiveness and sustainability of these initiatives.

Sources indicate that de facto mega-prisons — that is, overcrowded prisons with excessive inmate populations — existed in Latin America long before Bukele, says criminologist Jose Luis Perez Guadalupe, former president of the National Penitentiary Institute and former interior minister in Peru. Lurigancho Prison in Lima, for example, designed to hold 3,000 inmates, has housed nearly 11,000 for decades.

But ever since CECOT was debuted in 2023, the concept of a "mega-prison" has been primarily linked to maximum-security facilities. For Olga Espinoza, an academic specializing in prison systems at the School of Government of the University of Chile, this association is problematic because it implies that the entire prison population requires "extremely severe" punishment.

According to Espinoza, placing the entire prison population in maximum-security facilities would amount to inefficient and extremely costly "over-intervention." These facilities require substantial investments in infrastructure, technology, specialized staff, anti-corruption measures and social reintegration programs.

It would also be ineffective because "international evidence indicates that when people with different profiles are placed in the same space, there is a high risk of the spread of criminal behavior," the Chilean expert adds.

Several criminal groups across the region even have their roots in overcrowded prisons: Tren de Aragua in Venezuela; Los Lobos, Los Choneros and Los Tiguerones in Ecuador; and Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and Comando Vermelho (CV) in Brazil.

Even when the proposal involves simply building large-scale facilities, investing in a single structure may seem attractive given the difficulties of developing public infrastructure in Latin America.

However, "there is insufficient evidence to support the claim that building mega-prisons is more cost-effective," says Renato Rivera, a senior analyst at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC).

The United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners, adopted in 1955, "the recommendation has been to build medium-sized prisons housing between 1,000 and 2,000 inmates rather than mega-prisons," explains Perez Guadalupe, a professor at the Universidad del Pacifico in Lima.

Sources indicate that "Mega-prisons, apart from being impersonal, can become extremely dangerous," indicates Guadalupe. As an example, the GI-TOC's Rivera highlights the widely reported prison massacres in Ecuador in 2021 that took place in the country's largest and most populated facilities.

Experts acknowledge that mass incarceration has coincided with a dramatic decline in violence in El Salvador and has strengthened the public's perception of safety. Despite reports of arbitrary arrests, abuses and more than 500 deaths in state custody in the country, announcements of upcoming mega-prisons project an image of a strong state confronting organized crime across the region.

However, they warn that this political and symbolic impact does not guarantee sustainable results. Achieving them would require a "clear commitment" to external oversight, human rights protections and social reintegration programs, which governments have yet to demonstrate, Espinoza says.

Sources indicate that perez Guadalupe is particularly critical of the Salvadoran model, describing it as "pure propaganda." He believes the images released from CECOT violate human dignity. He also argues that the state must demonstrate "moral superiority over those who break the law.".

Although transnational organized crime represents a growing challenge across the region, the Peruvian criminologist considers El Salvador's case exceptional.

Following the mass arrests carried out under the state of emergency introduced by Bukele, the country has one of the highest incarceration rates in the world. CECOT was designed to permanently detain members of gangs such as MS-13 and Barrio 18, which are considered extremely dangerous.

Recent findings suggest that however, the reality of other Latin American prison systems is different. The question is not where to lock people deprived of their liberty away forever, but rather "how we want them to leave: worse or better," Perez Guadalupe argues, pointing out that most will eventually return to society.

According to recent reports, in theory, the official alternative is provided by the UN Nelson Mandela Rules for the treatment of prisoners, updated in 2015. They establish principles for modern prison management, including respect for human dignity, an absolute prohibition on torture and degrading treatment and social reintegration as a central goal of imprisonment.

In practice, Latin America has developed innovative approaches in this direction. These include the APAC model in Brazil, which operates facilities without guards, weapons or violence; Conflict Prevention and Resolution Committees in Argentina; and the Alternative Criminal Justice Center in the Mexican state of Sonora.

Experts also point to the need for maximum-security prisons for specific inmate profiles, but on a smaller scale and with more precise classification of the prison population.

Finally, they emphasize that prisons, including mega-prisons, primarily address the consequences of organized crime rather than its root causes. Poverty, social exclusion and a lack of opportunities require public policies focused on employment, education and social integration to reduce the conditions that enable crime to expand in one of the world's most unequal regions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic on Tuesday disclosed more details about the biggest investment agreements with major cloud providers Amazon and Google.
  • While we already knew that Amazon stood to make a killing on its Anthropic investments from the IPO, Anthropic revealed that Amazon’s total stake will come in at just shy of 15% (14.7% to be exact).
  • According to recent reports, even more interesting is that Amazon could have, if it wished, owned an even bigger share of the firm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic on Tuesday disclosed more details about the biggest investment agreements with major cloud providers Amazon and Google.

While we already knew that Amazon stood to make a killing on its Anthropic investments from the IPO, Anthropic revealed that Amazon’s total stake will come in at just shy of 15% (14.7% to be exact).

According to recent reports, even more interesting is that Amazon could have, if it wished, owned an even bigger share of the firm. When Amazon invested billions in Anthropic in 2023 and 2024 (long before Claude Code took the enterprise world by storm, back in the days when Anthropic looked like it would forever be a speck in OpenAI’s shadow), the cloud giant obtained promissory notes that could convert into equity.

These notes carry conversion prices of about $2.09 or $5.05 per share, depending on the year of investment. Amazon has opted to convert a chunk of them as part of the IPO into a special class of non-voting shares that will give it about 15% ownership. (The shares can receive dividends and convert to standard voting Class A shares when sold, the filing says.).

Sources indicate that but it has also opted to hold on to billions of dollars’ worth of the notes for now. If it converted them all right now, it would own just under 24% of Anthropic (23.8% to be precise).

It has been revealed that google, meanwhile, will own just under 14% (13.7%), also in non-voting shares, which come from the conversion of notes, as well as the “private placement” sale of shares as part of this IPO. A group of major tech companies (AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC Partners) have agreed to buy $26 billion worth of this non-voting stock. Google and Nvidia each agreed to buy $10 billion worth.

So while a lot of investors stand to make billions of dollars in Anthropic’s IPO, Amazon is one of the biggest winners, and that doesn’t even count what AWS stands to earn from Anthropic’s commitment to spend more than $100 billion on its cloud services over the next decade.

But he doesn’t think Claude is conscious.

But he doesn’t think Claude is conscious.

Sources indicate that microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled, at least when it comes to how AI might make startling changes to the structure of the economy and how politics might change because of it. “I am AGI-pilled in the sense that at an economy level, what is the political economy’s organization around AGI?” he asked at a roundtable discussion following his Microsoft Ignite keynote at the Chase Center in San Francisco.

But Nadella doesn’t think frontier models like Claude are conscious. “I don’t think so,” he said, adding that he follows Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman’s view that companies should not give rights to models and treat them like they might have a moral status, which companies like Anthropic do as a matter of principle. Suleyman has told me he thinks Anthropic’s team has “wireheaded” themselves, and that this approach is dangerous.

Nadella wasn’t quite as firm about it. “It’s a good debate,” he remarked. “I’m not sort of dogmatic about it. What I’m saying is the most crucial social technical issue we have to deal with is how do you ensure that an economy can diffuse this technology broadly?”.

Industry observers note that I asked Nadella how he was thinking about AI after hearing his response to another reporter’s questions about Anthropic releasing more products in its office suite. Nadella talked at length about the potential collapse of the economy and the end of democracy if one AI model were allowed to achieve monopoly status.

“If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us.”.

Industry observers note that “Most people think about this as a competition between tech firms, which of course it will be,” he said. “But remember, the model has no limits. It’ll be a healthcare company. It can be a financial services company. It can be anything if it wants to be. It can take over the government. Thinking of this as some narrow competition between tech firms, of who is going to get to the next trillion dollars of market cap, is one of the strangest, narrowest ways to think about it.”.

Nadella went on to say that the very nature of companies stood to be disrupted in the future. “If intelligence has network effects, what is the future of a firm?” he asked. “If the model sees anything and learns it, and essentially all of human capital collapses into token capital, what is the role of a firm and the human capital in a firm? That’s the debate.”.

Sources indicate that “I think the political economy is going to get more and more interesting in that context. No one — at least in a democracy — can even win an election if this just goes that way, if there’s only capital and there’s no labor. I mean, I don’t know, that’s not an economy.”.

Recent findings suggest that “If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us. Not just for me. You are also going to somehow be some affiliate of Anthropic.”.

Needless to say, this is not how tech CEOs usually talk about the launch of competing spreadsheet software.

Industry observers note that of course, Nadella was also promoting Microsoft’s various AI tools at Ignite, which promise to let enterprise clients pick the most cost-effective models for various tasks, run their own models, and control their own data in different ways. The idea here is that the market will demand many different kinds of models and sovereign data in order to keep control from centralizing, a theme Nadella kept coming back to as we spoke.

“I think that if you believe that the world, the economy needs more than one firm or two firms, then by definition there need to be as many models as firms of some sort,” he mentioned.

Ghana's upcoming $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (902 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The French-made Falcon 6X replaces the ageing presidential jet, officials say.
  • Ghana's government has defended its purchase of a new presidential jet amid criticism over its cost, as many citizens continue to struggle with the high cost of living.
  • The $60m (Â£46m) French-made Falcon 6X has sparked a political row, with opposition politicians accusing President John Mahama's administration of misplaced priorities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The French-made Falcon 6X replaces the ageing presidential jet, officials say.

Ghana's government has defended its purchase of a new presidential jet amid criticism over its cost, as many citizens continue to struggle with the high cost of living.

The $60m (Â£46m) French-made Falcon 6X has sparked a political row, with opposition politicians accusing President John Mahama's administration of misplaced priorities.

But the government claims the purchase is justified, arguing that Ghana's improving economy makes the aircraft affordable and is needed to replace an ageing presidential jet.

The controversy comes as Mahama's administration seeks to demonstrate an economic recovery after years of financial difficulties that forced Ghana to seek IMF assistance.

Can Ghana's new president meet the voters' high expectations?

Manufactured by French aerospace company Dassault Aviation, the aircraft was delivered to the Ghana Air Force on Monday at a reported cost of $61m.

Parliament approved its purchase last December as part of a broader programme to modernise Ghana's military aviation fleet, which also includes four helicopters from Airbus.

The jet was welcomed with a water salute on Monday, but its arrival triggered criticism online and among opposition politicians over the cost and timing of the purchase.

While in the opposition, Mahama himself opposed buying a newly introduced presidential jet, prompting questions about why his administration has now gone head with the purchase.

Opposition MP Samuel Abu Jinapor questioned the government's priorities, saying the expenditure came at a time when many Ghanaians continue to struggle with the cost of living and youth unemployment remained alarmingly high.

"What was unacceptable in opposition cannot suddenly become acceptable in government merely because the occupants of power have changed," Jinapor added.

He accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of hypocrisy, recalling how its senior figures had strongly opposed proposals for a new presidential aircraft when they were in opposition.

Jinapor also called for greater transparency over the procurement process, how the purchase was financed and the government's justification for the expenditure.

Defence Minister Kenneth Adjei welcomed and inspected the newly introduced jet on Monday.

The purchase has also prompted sharp criticism on social media, with some owners arguing the money could have been spent on more pressing public needs.

"This money can employ over 100,000 nurses and 200,000 teachers," an X user posted.

But the government has rejected the criticism, saying Ghana's economic circumstances have changed considerably since the NDC opposed a similar purchase.

Peter Lanchene Toobu, chairman of parliament's defence committee, said the party had never opposed acquiring a presidential jet in principle.

Its objection, he noted, had been on the timing when Ghana was experiencing severe economic difficulties.

"We agreed in principle that we needed to purchase a upcoming presidential jet," he noted.

He argued, however, that Ghana could not justify the expenditure at a time when it was seeking a $3bn bailout from the IMF.

"The strength and macroeconomic stability of this country have enhanced our status in the sense that imports have become cheaper, and this is the right time," he added.

Toobu stated the government had purchased the aircraft without borrowing, citing a stronger Ghanaian currency and improved economic conditions.

Government spokesperson Kwakye Ofosu also dismissed suggestions that the purchase was a misplaced priority.

He pointed to falling prices of construction materials and lower borrowing costs as evidence of the country's improved economic situation.

"When I was campaigning in 2024, and I was donating cement, it cost 115 cedis (Â£7.5) a bag. Today, for 80 cedis, you will get a bag of cement," he told JoyNews.

The controversy has also extended to the aircraft's interior, following claims that it has a dedicated bedroom and bathroom.

But Ofosu dismissed claims that the jet had such luxury facilities, saying the president has no intention of "bathing in the air".

Industry observers note that "There certainly is no bathroom. President Mahama has no intention of bathing in the air," Ofosu said.

He explained that the jet has reclining seats that can be converted into sleeping arrangements but denied that it has a dedicated bedroom.

The government says the new jet will replace the 16-year-old Falcon 900EX, which has suffered recurring maintenance problems, including corrosion and leakages in its fuel tank.

The older jet was reportedly grounded in France for several months in 2025 while undergoing repairs.

Officials say the Falcon 6X has a longer flying range, reducing the need for refuelling stops on international trips and improving the reliability of presidential travel.

Professor Godfred Alufar Bokpin, an economist at the University of Ghana noted that while the president's safety was paramount, the timing of the purchase was difficult to justify amid severe austerity measures, high unemployment and widespread infrastructure challenges.

"The timing makes it a bit difficult to understand," he told the BBC, adding that the government should provide a cost-benefit analysis explaining why buying the jet was preferable to leasing one and how the decision serves Ghana's interests.

Additional reporting by Thomas Naadi in Accra.

#23761. Latest Update: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Ars Technica review

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2354 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Ars Technica review

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2354 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just a minute ago, I was shooting my way out of a cocaine deal gone wrong, darting behind furniture for cover.
  • This is the contrast at the heart of Grand Theft Auto VI, a game that seems to revel in both action movie bombast and the mundanities of everyday life for an up-and-coming young criminal couple.
  • It has been revealed that the reimagined and expanded Vice City is still the grand, crude, satirical criminal playground you’d expect after 25 years of 3D Grand Theft Auto games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just a minute ago, I was shooting my way out of a cocaine deal gone wrong, darting behind furniture for cover. Now I’m sitting on the floor of my home, working through the instructions to construct an Ikea-style coffee table with my partner. A tiny heart with a plus sign pops up, showing that our relationship is stronger for this quotidian domestic effort.

This is the contrast at the heart of Grand Theft Auto VI, a game that seems to revel in both action movie bombast and the mundanities of everyday life for an up-and-coming young criminal couple.

It has been revealed that the reimagined and expanded Vice City is still the grand, crude, satirical criminal playground you’d expect after 25 years of 3D Grand Theft Auto games. And that world is as full, detailed, technically impressive, and polished as you would expect after this latest installment received a reported billion-dollar budget and roughly a decade of development work involving thousands of Rockstar staffers.

But it’s the scenes between the over-the-top and somewhat repetitive action scenes that really make this Grand Theft Auto stand out. Almost every explosive gunfight or high-speed car chase is counterpointed by a sublimely dull, lightly interactive moment of mere routine existence: grilling burgers with pals by the water, playing fetch with a random dog, helping a neighbor tune up a car, or joking around over 18 holes of mini golf.

It has been revealed that taken together, the juxtaposition lends a sense of surreal hyperreality to the goings-on in Vice City and its environs. Each of the game’s two sides gives the other a chance to breathe, forming a series of emotional peaks and valleys that stretch across a truly gargantuan amount of detailed simulation and pure gaming content.

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto VI never lets you get too settled with a budding life of crime or a budding family life. And it’s all the better for it.

Sources indicate that A large part of why this works so well is Jason and Lucia, the dual protagonists whose relationship drives the story. While that relationship starts off a bit awkwardly—thanks chiefly to Lucia’s brief prison stint—it quickly develops into a true criminal and life partnership. Both sides of the relationship are driven by a mutual desire to move up in the criminal world and eventually settle down to a legit family life, if they can just earn enough from the next significant score.

In a recent development, of the two, Jason is definitely the duller partner. An ex-military meathead with a ripped body and a dull, affect-free vocal delivery, a decent chunk of Jason’s lines essentially boil down to “Yeah, sure, that’s fine.” While the game struggles to expose a bit of a tender and thoughtful side hiding underneath Jason’s cool demeanor, the writing can’t quite break through the emotionless masculine facade that Jason wears as a semi-permanent mask.

Recent findings suggest that lucia is much more interesting as a vivacious and amiable Latina eager to grab any opportunity presented to her. The game takes some time to dig into the difficulties of Lucia’s underprivileged youth and highlight her strained relationship with an unreliable mother, helping to add some important depth to her chip-on-her-shoulder journey of self-improvement. And even the boring Jason seems that much more appealing seen through the lens of Lucia’s good-natured teasing and genuine affection.

It has been revealed that while Jason and Lucia can and do operate independently—and the game lets you change between them frequently—it’s their moments of togetherness that really stand out. There’s an easy, rom-com comfort to their time together, whether they’re discussing their future on the couch (“I feel like I haven’t done anything normal in a minute”), taking some time for quick romance (the game cuts away before things get too hot and heavy), or laying down covering fire for each other during a firefight (the lack of a co-op mode for these missions feels truly baffling).

In a recent development, there’s a minor relationship simulation component to the game, with a simple “heart level” that can rise or fall based on some basic decisions. Don’t expect a lot of dating-sim style drama, though; as long as you make the completely obvious choices when they’re presented, it’s hard to let the relationship fall apart. That’s a good thing, too, because this is a relationship that’s easy to root for, even when the participants are literally getting away with murder.

Industry observers note that in true Grand Theft Auto fashion, Jason and Lucia’s particular way of chasing The American Dream is through a life of crime. Their travels through the criminal underworld start off kind of slow, as Lucia’s begging gradually compels Jason to reluctantly introduce her to the two-bit operators with which he’s found himself involved.

For the first half of the game, the pair are constantly interacting with a rogues’ gallery of latest criminal acquaintances, each more over-the-top than the last, and all of them having specific needs that somehow only Jason and Lucia can fulfill. Many of the missions these small-time crooks have on offer end up feeling like the criminal equivalent of errands—drive here, take that, lose the cops, repeat.

And while a few standout characters develop complex interpersonal relationships with Jason and Lucia over multiple missions, most of these early side characters feel like one-note caricatures that can be distilled to a few tropey traits.

It isn’t until the back half of the game that the main storyline really starts to focus on what it does best: integrating Jason and Lucia into a persistent ring of professional criminals working toward bigger and bigger scores. Here, the missions build on each other, with characters going undercover, casing targets, and learning new skills that eventually come together in some truly tense and bombastic heists. These missions also do the best job of showing off the dual protagonist system, frequently shifting the perspective between Jason and Lucia to highlight their different skills and views on how things are going down.

Recent findings suggest that outside of this core plot, though, many of the missions and side stories in GTA VI make Jason and Lucia feel like side characters in their own story. I found myself beginning to tune out during some of the many missions in which one or both protagonists serve as glorified security props or overpaid getaway drivers amid other characters’ contrived turf wars. And even dozens of hours into the game, there were still missions that felt like tutorials, seemingly built around the opportunity to introduce some newly introduced simulation system or control scheme.

Through it all, the game can’t seem to totally shake the style of sophomoric humor that feels a lot less “edgy” today than it did when Grand Theft Auto III hit back in 2001 (for players who are old enough to remember that release, at least). There are countless extended bits where the entire joke seems to boil down to “Man, kinky sex is weird, isn’t it?” or “Hey look, it’s a male penis (or something that looks similar to one).” And the game seems to take particular pleasure in forcing Jason into uncomfortable situations with plenty of T&A, much to Lucia’s good-natured bemusement.

A word of warning for parents: This is a game that definitely earns a hard “M for Mature” rating and indicates how standards for that rating have shifted since GTA: San Andreas earned an AO re-rating for hiding a single sex scene amid its legacy code.

In a recent development, there are moments where GTA VI’s satire cuts a bit deeper. I especially liked a couple of side stories that skewered buzzword-spewing crypto bros and multi-level marketing schemes with some welcome over-the-top excess. Overall, though, the game’s warmed-over one-liner takes on “wokeness” felt about as fresh as jokes about mothers-in-law and TV dinners, without much in the way of thought-provoking statements on society as a whole in 2026.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto VI has a gift for finding excuses to lure you into an expertly designed space and then throwing together a reason for why you have to shoot/punch your way out. That might sound snarky, but I actually mean it more or less sincerely; I was frequently surprised by the scenarios the writers dreamed up to turn what seemed like a routine trip to some beautiful locale into a firefight with way more armed goons than seems strictly necessary.

The moment-to-moment shooting will feel very familiar to Grand Theft Auto fans, by which I mean it’s dead simple to hide behind convenient cover and pop up to pick off relatively stupid enemies one by one with a dizzying array of available weaponry. The rare enemies that do manage to flank you seem to have incredibly bad aim, even at close range, and both Jason and Lucia can take a whole lot more punishment than the average quick-to-crumble grunt.

Driving around town is significantly more exciting—you’ll be darting between cars in heavy traffic to chase down antagonists, avoid the police, or simply get where you’re going faster. It’s still a blast to sample as many vehicles as you can, from zippy but easy-to-wreck sports cars to tank-like trucks that can plow through traffic, tiny motorbikes that can squeeze through tight spaces, and off-road vehicles that can explore off the beaten path.

Driving through the city also offers ample opportunities to get distracted from your main goals by dozens of side activities that dot the map. Even as I struggled to work through the story on deadline, I found myself getting sucked in for hours trying to master drone racing, chasing gold medals in countless mud-splattered rally races, or hunting for one of the many meditation spots hidden in out-of-the-way corners.

While most of these side activities offer money or improve character stats, some are simply there to be experienced. Completionists will have a bear of a time tracking down every single hidden collectible, rare car, robbable location, and beautiful landmark the developers have placed throughout the city. Grand Theft Auto VI seems set to be one of those games you can just load up to hang out in long after the main story missions are done.

Recent findings suggest that even with a fast vehicle, much of that “hang out” time can be spent simply crossing the game’s massive map. Getting from the depths of the wilderness in the north to the tip of the keys in the south is a six-plus-mile trip (measured at an apparently real-world-accurate scale) that can take 10 minutes to weave your way across on a good traffic day. During these cross-city treks, the tenor of the city’s architecture morphs noticeably as you pass from rich gated communities through the glitzy skyscraper-laden downtown and on to downtrodden neighborhoods, backwoods swamps, and laid-back island beach communities.

In a recent development, as nice as Vice City’s outdoor architecture is, GTA VI’s interiors are where the game’s developers really show off. Practically every story mission seems to introduce a new cavernous indoor space that’s fully furnished and lovingly crafted to look naturally lived-in and also utterly unlike anything you’ve seen before. And while you can’t go into every one of the thousands of buildings you pass on the streets of Vice City, you can enter a surprisingly large number, each with its own distinct layout and decorations.

Sources indicate that another element that makes all these spaces feel lived-in is the game’s surprisingly detailed crowd system. Grand Theft Auto VI sometimes packs over a hundred non-player characters into a single space, with no two characters looking or acting alike in size, shape, dress, or animation. Working your way through these crowds can be integral to some of the game’s missions, but even when you’re just casually exploring, it’s fun to take advantage of eavesdropping opportunities, listening in on individual conversations that build into overlapping chatter (realistically muffled through walls and over distance).

Grand Theft Auto VI’s spaces also seem specifically designed to show off the game’s incredible lighting system, which really shines on a PS5 Pro. The effect is most apparent at night, when car headlights streaming through a window or the rotating blue-and-red of a cop car can cast the entire world in an otherworldly glow.

But even in “normal” lighting conditions, I’d occasionally find myself slack-jawed at the details: a laptop screen partially reflected in a character’s glasses, the way rotating pyrotechnic laser effects played across dancers in a crowded club, the fluttering shadows cast by a leafy tree near sunset, or the finger smudges visible on your cell phone in bright sunshine.

It has been revealed that I could go on and on about the little “attention to detail” touches that add up to a more engaging world simulation. Characters who fall in the dirt get dust on only the specific parts of their clothes that hit the ground. Older characters look distinctly wrinkly, with veins that show through their thinning skin. Fabric and hair flow naturally in the wind and as characters move. Rain beads on car roofs and drips off overhangs during a storm.

Through it all, one moment really stood out to me. As I prepared for an upcoming firefight, I had Lucia start eating some chips to buff her health. Halfway through the bag, I had her pick up a nearby soda, too. At first, Lucia held the chip bag in one hand and used the other to pick out individual chips. But once that other hand was occupied with a soda, she started shaking the bag above her head to pour the chips directly into her mouth.

Industry observers note that when I thought about the effort that went into coding and recording that specific animation for such a highly specific edge case, I thought about the millions of man-hours that went into making Grand Theft Auto VI the ultimate expression of this kind of urban crime/life sim. It might be a long time before we see this level of focused effort on a singular interactive vision again.

#23757. ‘It’s a risk’: How Rockstar built the most detailed (and romantic) GTA yet

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1283 w)
📖 Baca
