  • Representative Juan Vargas shared a photograph of the boy and his family in a social media post on Monda, writing: “11 days ago, an 8-year-old in San Diego was taken into federal custody during an immigration check-in.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Child reunited with family after he was detained by immigration agents in San Diego and transferred to Texas.

An eight-year-old Haitian boy who was put into restraints and detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November and transferred to a facility in Texas has been reunited with his family in California.

Representative Juan Vargas shared a photograph of the boy and his family in a social media post on Monda, writing: “11 days ago, an 8-year-old in San Diego was taken into federal custody during an immigration check-in. He was separated from his loved ones and held in a facility in Texas. Today, he’s finally home.”.

The Haitian Bridge Alliance, an immigration advocacy group, confirmed that the third-grader had been released from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody.

“An eight-year-old child belongs in a classroom, on a playground, and surrounded by love – not in immigration detention. We welcome his release, but his freedom should never have required a public outcry,” Guerline Jozef, executive director of the Haitian Bridge Alliance, noted in a statement.

The third-grader at Fay elementary school was put in restraints and taken into custody by federal immigration officers at a check-in earlier in the month, according to video obtained by NBC News and an oversight letter Democratic lawmakers sent to the Departments of Homeland Security and Health and Human Services.

A spokesperson for the homeland security department mentioned ICE took the child into custody “out of an abundance of caution and to ensure the child’s safety”.

The uncle, the spokesperson remarked in a statement to the Guardian, was unable to prove legal guardianship – and that officials were obliged by federal anti-trafficking laws to take the boy into care as an “unaccompanied alien child”.

The Haitian Bridge Alliance remarked the boy was in the care of his uncle and cousins after his father was deported last year.

Sources indicate that “I’m so grateful that he’s home, but this should have never happened in the first place,” Vargas remarked in a second social media post, adding that he would be asking the Trump administration for answers. While he was detained, the child was “held in a facility in Texas, far away from his home in San Diego”, Vargas said.

According to recent reports, celebrating the boy’s return, Jozef of the Haitian Bridge Alliance told NBC News: “The aunt was literally crying, and she remarked: ‘I have not eaten since the Wednesday they took my baby.’ They haven’t been able to sleep because of that.” She added: “The cousins were there when they took him, and wondering: will they ever see him again? But today [Monday] they are able to see him again. They are able to hug him.”.

#23736. Tesla’s $30,000 Cybercab comes with a $299 monthly catch

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (919 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla’s $30,000 Cybercab comes with a $299 monthly catch

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (919 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Or in the case of Tesla’s self-driving Cybercab, several.
  • Last Friday night, Tesla remarked it had invited “select customers” to purchase their very own Cybercabs.
  • From there, though, the Cybercab will need constant cash infusions to stay on the road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is always a catch. Or in the case of Tesla’s self-driving Cybercab, several.

Last Friday night, Tesla remarked it had invited “select customers” to purchase their very own Cybercabs. The two-seat, gold vehicle is unlike any other on the market: It lacks a steering wheel and brake pedals, and is primarily driven by software. (Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Alphabet’s Waymo and Amazon’s Zoox, offer self-driving rides on ride-hail networks, but don’t let people buy their cars.) Tesla’s “limited release” will supposedly offer some people (unclear how many) the opportunity to pay $29,900 to take delivery in December.

From there, though, the Cybercab will need constant cash infusions to stay on the road.

The business model raises questions about what people will actually get when they buy a Cybercab. “You’ll never really own the car,” says Ivan Drury, the director of insights at Edmunds. “It’s more like $30,000 to buy into a franchise.”.

According to recent reports, according to documents posted on Tesla’s website, the vehicle “will not operate” without what Tesla is calling an “autonomy subscription,” a monthly fee that will start at $299. If owners don’t pay on time and in full, their self-driving cars won’t work. If they try to operate the vehicles in areas that don’t support the service—right now, they’re restricted to portions of cities in Florida and Texas—their self-driving cars won’t work. (That area can expand, contract, or “relocate” at any time.).

If owners do anything that Tesla deems “unauthorized or inappropriate,” the organization notes it can suspend or cancel the subscription—and their self-driving cars won’t work. If the vehicle loses connectivity, the self-driving cars won’t work. (“Tesla is not responsible for carrier, spectrum, environmental, or other external outages,” its “autonomy agreement” says.).

Tesla also reserves the right to make an owner’s car not work at any time: It says it can, for any safety or security purpose, suspend or terminate access to Cybercab tech, or restrict operations by location, road type, weather, or “condition.” This is particularly salient because the Cybercab is also under investigation by US safety regulators, who are trying to understand why Tesla believes the vehicle meets safety standards without so many of the parts and systems required.

Tesla didn’t respond to a request for comment.

Sources indicate that for years, automakers have seen increasingly software-dominated vehicles as an opportunity to get drivers hooked on the same special sauce that makes Netflix, Amazon, and Spotify so potent: monthly subscription services. Because these vehicles can receive over-the-air software updates, manufacturers can offer drivers upcoming services as they make them. The upside is high, tech-style margins that keep rolling in, versus the razor-thin ones seen in car-making. A 2024 report suggested that connected-car features could one day be a $200 billion industry.

In a recent development, in some ways, the subscription model is working. Today, some automakers charge extra for remote start, security, Internet connectivity, and advanced driver assistance features. General Motors said it made $2.7 billion in subscription-related revenue last year from fees drivers paid for its OnStar and Super Cruise services.

But some customers have also found the business model yucky, or even offensive. Why charge extra to “unlock” a feature that’s already built into a car? If an automaker can add a new feature at any time, can’t they also take it away? And if they can take it away, what does “ownership” mean? In 2022, BMW told drivers in select countries it would activate factory-installed heated seats for a monthly or one-time fee; it eventually backed down after public outcry, pledging the company would no longer charge subscription fees for preinstalled hardware. (BMW is still pursuing a subscription model for some features.) “Consumers hate being nickel-and-dimed for subscriptions,” notes Drury.

According to recent reports, tesla was an early mover in the subscription feature space and has offered connectivity and driver-assistance features for monthly or one-time fees for a decade. As the organization has shifted away from making cars and toward robotics and autonomous vehicles, executives have made clear that charging for services is the future. (Its Robotaxi service at the moment picks up fare-paying passengers in parts of eight US cities.) So Tesla buyers may be particularly amenable to paying monthly to make their self-driving cars go.

Industry observers note that in exchange for monthly fees, buyers will also get access to other services, too, including remote support, roadside assistance, tire, air filter, and windshield wiper replacements, and tire and camera inspections. (The agreement says that list might change, too.) Cybercabs will be able to “travel autonomously, unoccupied to a Tesla service center,” the company says. The fee doesn’t cover insurance.

Cybercab buyers will have other restrictions. The vehicle is for personal use only. Even though CEO Elon Musk has repeatedly said owners will be able to put their vehicles on Tesla’s wider Robotaxi network to make money during downtime, and even has an online interest form for those who want to own and operate their own Cybercab fleets, the current ownership agreement prohibits that. Buyers are also prohibited from selling or transferring their vehicles without Tesla’s written consent. The tech giant “advises against” children under 13 riding in the Cybercab, and prohibits children from riding without an adult present.

In a post on X, Musk indicated no apparent compunction about the Cybercab business model, but did say the monthly price for autonomy “is too high.” He wrote that the price should be “more like ~$115/month.”.

Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang’s ouster

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending the organization’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S.
  • China’s access to leading AI accelerators was an important topic during the company’s first earnings call since CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down last week.
  • Sources indicate that nvidia’s deal to sell H200 chips in China was brokered by Huang and President Donald Trump.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending the organization’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.

China’s access to leading AI accelerators was an important topic during the company’s first earnings call since CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down last week. The disclosure comes the same day Nvidia declared it was creating a board-level committee to oversee national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks.

Sources indicate that nvidia’s deal to sell H200 chips in China was brokered by Huang and President Donald Trump. The arrangement required the chips to be shipped through the U.S., allowing the government to collect a 25% tariff.

The pathway angered China hawks who wanted to deny Chinese labs computing power and maintain the United States’ lead in AI, but Huang long argued that it was more crucial for the U.S. to compete in China. In April, he told podcaster Dwarkesh Patel that “to concede that market for the United States technology industry is a disservice to our country.”.

Huang’s ouster — in part over an affair with the CEO of a tech giant under investigation for smuggling chips into China — has coincided with latest rules, issued Monday, barring advanced U.S. chips from foreign data centers that serve Chinese customers remotely.

Investment bank Jefferies forecast that those rules might trim between $44 billion and $62 billion from Nvidia’s data center revenue next year. Referencing the newly introduced export controls, Kress noted that the backlog of demand for advanced chips like Vera Rubin means the rules would have no impact on the organization’s top-line revenue.

Industry observers note that in the long term, the manufacturer may face the loss of potential customers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia. Critics of Nvidia’s dependence on China claim that as much as 20% of its revenue comes from demand linked to the country — annual revenue at its Singapore subsidiary hit $104 billion in 2025 before Nvidia stopped disclosing those figures — but that’s clearly going to change.

Recent findings suggest that even before Nvidia decided to stop shipping H200s, China had largely refused to accept their delivery. The government would prefer to generate demand for the country’s domestic chip industry, even if major AI compute users want the still-superior Nvidia equipment, according to Jacob Feldgoise, a researcher at Georgetown’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology.

Meanwhile, Chinese frontier labs are finding ways to access Nvidia chips elsewhere. All of China’s leading AI models show evidence of having been trained on Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips that are prohibited from being exported to China.

That training may have taken place at data centers outside of China, but sales to those facilities will be barred under the new rules. If large data centers suited for training AI models want to buy Nvidia chips, they will have to certify they aren’t serving any Chinese customers, export control attorney Dan Fisher-Owens told TechCrunch.

If they can’t provide that certification, the latest rules may force them toward other chip options and further eat into Nvidia’s market share.

Tech Report: Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (912 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: The Verge

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • More than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V was first released, its sequel is finally launching.
  • Sources indicate that part of this has to do with the success of its predecessor, as GTA V sold more than 230 million copies over the last 13 years.
  • But GTA VI is now a real thing you can play, and you can also keep track of all of the important post-launch information right here.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V was first released, its sequel is finally launching. On November 19th, GTA VI will be available on both the PS5 and Xbox Series X / S, and it’s quite possibly the most anticipated video game launch of all time.

Sources indicate that part of this has to do with the success of its predecessor, as GTA V sold more than 230 million copies over the last 13 years. Some of it has to do with the sheer length of time between releases, a period that was plagued by leaks and a handful of delays that made the wait even harder for fans.

But GTA VI is now a real thing you can play, and you can also keep track of all of the important post-launch information right here. That includes our own review and interviews with the development team, as well as news on just how the game ends up resonating with players.

Industry observers note that lost in the excitement of GTA VI finally launching is the fact that Rockstar employees are in the process of voting on whether or not to unionize. Developer Nestor Uriarte explains the importance of the moment in an essay in The Guardian:.

In a recent development, winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that. As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry – one in which workers’ voices are taken into account more.

In a recent development, now that reviews have dropped for the game, it has skyrocketed to the top of Metacritic’s highest-rated list, surpassing Ocarina of Time (the original, not the remake). Of course, this could change as more reviews trickle in, but for now it’s safe to say that GTA VI was worth the long wait.

Grand Theft Auto VI isn’t just the biggest GTA game to date; it’s also the most romantic. Though the series is well known for its sordid assortment of criminal leads, GTA VI switches things up by starring a pair of thieves who also happen to fall in love after meeting while stealing a car. It’s still an open-world action game full of chaos and mayhem. But many players will also be attempting to nurture the budding relationship in between heists. The sprawling game is designed to support both audiences.

According to recent reports, “It’s a risk,” explains Rob Nelson, producer on GTA VI and co-studio head at developer Rockstar North. “It’s a real change for Grand Theft Auto. You can still play it the old way, you can reject all of this stuff. But for people who do engage, it’s meaningful — you’re earning it, you’re working at it, just like in a normal relationship.”.

According to recent reports, how do you follow a game like Grand Theft Auto V? Thirteen years ago, Rockstar’s crime-fueled epic went on to redefine what an open-world game could be and became an enormous success, selling more than 230 million copies across three generations of game consoles. It sits just behind Tetris and Minecraft on the list of the best-selling games of all time, and its lucrative online mode has helped it remain popular for well over a decade.

In a recent development, that level of success has allowed Rockstar to take its time with a sequel, which has further increased the hype around the next GTA. A series of major leaks and delays only exacerbated this. At a time when much of the video game industry is struggling, the next edition of GTA stands alone, a cultural moment so major (almost) everybody has been forced to get out of the way. The buildup to Grand Theft Auto VI’s launch is unlike anything the game industry has ever seen.

Sony has confirmed the 1.267GB download is mandatory to play the latest Grand Theft Auto when it introduces at midnight tonight. As with most PlayStation firmware patches, we don’t know what it does though, beyond “some security fixes to the system software.”.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar hasn’t publicly remarked who is playing the two leads in GTA VI, but The Game Awards’ nominee video claims that Manni L. Perez has been nominated for Best Performance for her work in the game.

GTA VI earned eight nominations, the most of any title, including one for Game of the Year.

Arion Kurtaj, a member of the Lapsus$ cybercrime group who leaked 90 videos of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022 and hacked other significant companies, pleaded guilty on Monday, according to the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS).

Kurtaj, who is now 21, hacked BT/EE sometime between August and November 2021, and starting in early November of that year, the organization “noted a marked increase in unauthorised SIM swaps of their customers mobile phones.” He was charged for those offenses and moved to a hotel for his “own protection” in September 2022, but “breached his bail conditions to carry out further hacks on major companies using a mobile phone, the hotel TV’s Wi-Fi and a firestick,” including hacks on Rockstar Games, Uber, and Revolut, the CPS indicates.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A video showing a young girl crying as she spoke about alleged police brutality during the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protests in July.
  • These are among the examples of content that have recently been restricted on social media in India.
  • Content creator CitySavitri describes herself as a "nobody" in the world of social media.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A video showing a young girl crying as she spoke about alleged police brutality during the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protests in July. A video examining the Hindu nationalist Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh's (RSS) contribution to the rise of India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). A satirical cartoon criticizing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.

These are among the examples of content that have recently been restricted on social media in India.

Content creator CitySavitri describes herself as a "nobody" in the world of social media. She had started making videos just two months ago and had around 600 followers on Instagram.

Recent findings suggest that yet a video looking at the RSS's role in the BJP's 2014 election victory was restricted in India within an hour of being posted. It was the first of three videos she posted that faced restrictions.

The experience made her feel that "anti-government commentary" was being monitored and curtailed.

"It is very plain and simple to understand," the content creator told DW.

Independent journalist Sadhika Tiwari was covering the CJP protest in Latest Delhi on July 20, when police used batons and tear gas against demonstrators.

Tiwari's video of a frightened young girl crying and speaking about police brutality garnered around 10 million views within hours, she said, before it was restricted in India.

Political cartoonist Satish Acharya has also faced repeated restrictions, with Instagram blocking his profile twice recently.

In May 2025, during the conflict between India and Pakistan, independent digital news outlet Maktoob Media's X account was withheld in India while it was reporting on the escalating crisis, its founder and editor Aslah Kayyalakkath told DW.

"We received no official notice or email from either the government or X. It was our readers who first alerted us to the blocking," he remarked.

Recent findings suggest that maktoob Media noted it contacted Indian officials and X but received no response. Access to the account was restored a few days later, again without an explanation.

Industry observers note that kayyalakkath noted Maktoob's content from the July protest also faced restrictions. "Suppressing independent journalism undermines transparency, accountability and democratic values," he said.

Several of the content creators and journalists interviewed by DW said they received no prior notification or explanation for the restrictions.

Some owners were not sure if their content had been blocked at the government's request or proactively by the social media platforms.

When asked for comment, Meta, the parent organization of Facebook and Instagram, pointed DW to a website statement noting users can appeal content and account restrictions.

Recent findings suggest that at the heart of the debate are India's IT Rules, 2021, amended in February 2026. Section 79 of India's IT Act protects social media platforms and other intermediaries from liability for content posted by third parties, provided they meet certain legal conditions.

One such requirement, introduced through the February 2026 amendments, is to remove or disable access to specified unlawful content within three hours of receiving a valid court order or a reasoned government notice. The previous deadline was 36 hours.

Failure to comply can result in intermediaries losing their liability protection.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The government's Sahyog portal, which coordinates takedown requests between law enforcement, platforms and telecom providers, has faced criticism over the pace at which notices are issued.

According to recent reports, meta said it uses automated tools and technologies to detect and review content that may violate its community standards. It also automatically restricts access to certain types of content in India to comply with legal requirements under the IT rules.

Pranesh Prakash, a technology law and policy adviser, said the amended rules allow authorized police officials to notify intermediaries about content they consider unlawful without necessarily filing a formal complaint or initiating other legal proceedings.

According to recent reports, "This has led to the worst period of social media censorship that India has ever seen, with digital news media accounts being blocked, cartoonists' accounts being blocked, and even mere discussions of an opposition leader's memoirs being blocked," he remarked. "Clearly, none of these disclosed any 'unlawful acts.'".

Prakash also raised concerns about the lack of public information on government requests to remove content, saying this made it difficult to assess the scale of restrictions.

The Software Freedom Law Center, India (SFLC.in), a digital rights organization, noted the growing reliance on automated takedowns raised serious concerns about transparency, accountability and due process.

"There is little transparency about the processes through which content is identified, flagged and restricted, or whether there is any meaningful human oversight before a takedown is implemented," SFLC.in told DW.

Industry observers note that the organization also tested X's verification process by submitting a takedown request against one of its own posts using a fake email address. X registered the request, raising questions about how it verified the identity and authority of those submitting requests.

After SFLC.in alerted the company, X introduced email verification codes for people submitting takedown requests.

"A channel that lets anyone pose as a law enforcement official can be misused to silence lawful speech," SFLC.in stated.

X did not respond to DW's request for a comment.

The Indian government denies that it is censoring online content.

While the ministry did not respond to DW's latest request for a comment, in an email response to DW in August, Vinod Kumar, chief of media and communications at the Information Technology Ministry, stated Instagram posts by students and protesters following the July CJP protests "are not being taken down as alleged.".

Industry observers note that "Media enjoys freedom in India. The Government does not censor online content," Kumar stated, adding that the government only acts against "objectionable content.".

Under the Indian IT rules, "unlawful content" generally refers to material which could threaten India's sovereignty and integrity, disturb public order, incite violence, or constitute defamation.

Industry observers note that however, social media influencers such as university professor Madri Kakoti, alias Dr. Medusa, continue to report restrictions. Kakoti's Instagram account was restricted in India on November 16 without notice, she said, along with that of satirist Shamita Yadav.

Rights groups including Human Rights Watch have warned that expanding content restrictions could chill free expression and encourage self-censorship among journalists, creators and ordinary users.

Acharya, however, mentioned he would continue his work.

"The Indian Constitution gives me the right to draw political cartoons," he said. "It's totally democratic to question and criticize the government in India.".

For Tiwari, the issue goes beyond the reach of a single video. It is also about preserving a record of what happened, after the Delhi Police denied allegations of using excessive force during the July 20 protest in front of the Supreme Court.

"We have seen several other videos now, and it's well established why that girl was crying, and that the Delhi Police used force and lied about it," she remarked.

"Still, I want that video back up because it needs to stay for posterity. I think that's the larger idea: they want to take this stuff down so it fades from memory, allowing them to categorically deny it later when we have little left to show for what happened.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jensen Huang and Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress.

Nvidia has firmly ruled out letting ousted co-founder Jensen Huang return as it revealed that sales doubled to more than $100bn.

In the tech giant's first results since Huang's dramatic exit last week, covering the three month period just before the recent scandal surfaced, interim chief executive Colette Kress said it was "business as usual". She told investors: "We've got this.".

Earlier on Tuesday, Huang said he would be "honoured" to return and lead Nvidia, having quit following alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected spy for China.

But Nvidia's chair Harvey Jones said: "The board does not intend to reinstate him.".

Nvidia reported that sales for the three months to 25 October rose to $115.8bn (Â£86.9bn), with shares in the tech giant jumping by 4.8% in after-hours trading.

The manufacturer's profits also doubled from a year ago rising to $65bn. Sales from data centres, a significant part of Nvidia's business, also doubled to $107bn.

The company said its rapid growth is poised to continue and revenue will rise by another 13% in the next quarter.

How important are Nvidia and Jensen Huang to the US economy?

Given the uncertainty surrounding the firm after Huang's exit, financial analysts had been unsure that Nvidia would provide any forward-looking guidance.

Daniela Hathorn, a senior analyst for trading platform Capital.com, said Nvidia's results "offer a strong answer to concerns that demand for AI infrastructure is cooling" and temper immediate worries that Huang was irreplaceable as a leader.

"The harder question is whether Nvidia can preserve the strategic advantage Huang helped build," Hathorn added. "His exit is unlikely to change orders already committed, but could matter more when Nvidia makes its next round of decisions on products, partnerships and investment.".

Watch: Who is suspected Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia affair investigation?

Kress seemed eager to stress that Nvidia can continue to not only succeed, but lead the ongoing AI buildout that is happening throughout the technology industry.

According to recent reports, "It is business as usual," she said. "Our partners, our suppliers, all of them are 100% behind us.".

She added that Nvidia's leadership team has "stood up very strongly over the last week... working seamlessly in all of their departments and projects".

Sources indicate that "Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed." Kress noted before leaving the analyst call. "We've got this.".

The interim chief executive also remarked Nvidia is no longer shipping Hopper data centre semiconductors to China.

The Hopper technology is in Nvidia's advanced H200 processors, which the firm won approval to sell in China after Huang's repeated lobbying efforts in Washington.

They had previously been restricted over concerns that selling them to China would give its industries and military an edge over the US.

Kress did not elaborate on why the shipments had been stopped.

The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal.

Jensen Huang states he would be 'honoured' to return as Nvidia CEO if board asked him.

Jones saying earlier that the firm would not answer analysts' questions about Huang or Nvidia's investigation into his conduct, he did address the search for a permanent replacement.

He remarked Nvidia is working with an executive search firm and is considering internal and external candidates, but that the organization would not rush its selection.

"With the advanced technology and the national security dynamics in the marketplace, our new chief executive will have to navigate those waters carefully," Jones remarked. "The search will be thorough and we want to do it as promptly as possible, but we won't do it before we find the exact right person.".

Michael Monaghan from investment firm Founder ETFs is among those who want Huang back in the top job at Nvidia.

The Nvidia investor told the BBC that he is waiting to see the results of a thorough investigation into Huang's actions, instead of relying on "salacious allegations" made in the media.

Nvidia's strong earnings are "from the machine that Jensen built" and a tech giant tends to lose "its shine and vision" after an iconic founder leaves, Monaghan said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Indigenous Awá people of Amazon make contact with villagers and accept food to take back to territory.

About 20 Indigenous people emerged from isolation in Brazil’s Amazon rainforest, several organizations reported on Tuesday, raising the alarm about increased invasions into the tribe’s territory.

According to the NGO Survival International, members of the Awá people, who live in voluntary isolation, arrived on Monday in a village and made contact with a government team in a “historic encounter”.

The village they entered was within the Arariboia Indigenous territory in the north-eastern state of Maranhão, home to the Guajajara ethnic group.

Local community leaders said the villagers offered food to the group.

“They asked for yams and took them back into their forest,” mentioned Survival International.

The NGO explained that the Awá typically subsist on hunting and gathering. However, they have faced increased incursions from illegal loggers, hunters and cattle ranchers.

A video of the encounter, filmed by Guajajara villagers and released by Survival International, highlights a group of men, women and children at the edge of the forest.

Partially concealed by vegetation, they appear naked and are wearing necklaces. The men carry bows and long arrows.

“The physical condition of some members, particularly the children and the elderly, caused concern among the villagers, who noted clear signs of severe emaciation,” warned Coapima, an organization representing Indigenous groups in Maranhão.

Coapima highlighted the risks that unplanned contact poses to such groups, noting that they are particularly “exposed to diseases” against which they have little to no immunity.

Funai, the public agency responsible for Indigenous affairs, remarked in a statement sent to AFP that its technical teams were closely monitoring the situation and analyzing available information regarding the group’s health.

Survival International’s director, Caroline Pearce, said the group’s choice to emerge from isolation was a “troubling indication of how the continued invasion of uncontacted peoples’ forests puts otherwise self-sufficient Indigenous people in real danger”.

She stated the Awá were being driven into “an ever-smaller island of the Amazon rainforest, surrounded by destruction”.

According to the NGO, about 196 “uncontacted” peoples and groups, who choose to live in isolation, have been identified across 10 countries.

More than 90% of such groups live in the Amazon rainforest, primarily in Brazil, with others in Indonesia and India.

The Forest Guardians – a group of Guajajara people who have battled illegal invasions for years – warned in comments in the Survival International statement that “climate change, fires, deforestation and land encroachment” were affecting the Awá’s way of life.

According to Survival International, many of the guardians have lost their lives trying to protect the territory they share with the Awá.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Europe is home to many of the world’s fastest growing companies of all time, veteran VC firm Atomico highlighted in its latest annual State of European Tech report.

In a recent development, the report, for instance, notes that the likes of Black Forest Labs and Microagi have reached $100 million in revenue in months, not years. “I think we can put to bed the idea that there’s a fundamental reason or constraint on the ability to scale a breakout company from here in Europe,” Atomico partner and head of intelligence Tom Wehmeier (pictured) told TechCrunch.

In a recent development, yet, there’s still more that the VC firm founded by Skype’s Niklas Zennström would like to see — and its call this year is for Europe to “build it” and “scale it,” but also “own it.” That’s a way of wishing these companies will remain European longer. But there’s also a sense that this success hasn’t been acknowledged enough, perhaps obscured by louder calls for improvements.

Wehmeier, the report’s lead author, was quick to opine that “policy, procurement and capital are not moving at the same speed as our founders.” But he remarked the tech sector should advocate for itself in an inspiring way.

“When it comes to policy, I think the language needs to be, ‘Hey, this is not us complaining. This is us saying here is an opportunity to make the magnitude of impact even greater,’” Wehmeier remarked. “When we frame it as problems, that becomes harder.”.

This reframing may also help European tech improve its image abroad, where complaints around overregulation may have overshadowed Europe’s potential to leverage its deep tech talent and growing pool of repeat entrepreneurs to have even more of success stories.

Plenty could be still done to fully unlock this potential, and Wehmeier said that “the next few weeks are going to be a really important test, with EU Inc.” Also known as the 28th regime, this initiative would create a unified European corporate regime akin to the Delaware C Corp.

In a recent development, if the last stretch of EU Inc’s grassroots campaign achieves it goal, it will become much easier to create and operate businesses across the EU. It would also show that the tech system got itself heard, which could open the door to the kind of endorsement Atomico is hoping to see more of.

Politicians have strong incentives to give the tech sector what it wants. If it is Europe’s second largest sector, biggest contributor to growth, and biggest job creator, “Do we not want more of that?” Wehmeier asked rhetorically. But it is unclear whether it will win them any votes.

In a recent development, to make the answer more straightforward, the tech sector will have to work on having public opinion on its side. For Wehmeier, one key is to “demonstrate that this is translating into value for citizens.”.

The report is supporting this endeavor with a mix of high-level data and examples from its portfolio; for instance, it notes that ICEYE’s satellites monitor severe weather, flooding, and other hazards; and Daniel Ek’s Neko Health has now done more than 100,000 body scans, some of which helped identify severe or life-threatening health conditions.

One limit to this argument is that Neko Health’s scans will seem pricey to most Europeans, who largely rely on collective, public health insurance. But Atomico seems to hope that its report will give readers FOMO not just as potential customers, but also as potential shareholders.

There’s more to be done for this to happen. Beyond joining the sector’s push for an EU capital markets union, he hopes more of Europe’s institutional investors will invest in the region’s own tech companies. “We must get to the place where Europe and European beneficiaries are the biggest shareholders in the success that we create,” Wehmeier noted.

Industry observers note that before that can happen, the industry must overcome anti-industry beliefs like fears of AI-induced job destruction. But Wehmeier is a believer in the power of proof. “I think that trust is going to be earned through showing results to the public — be that lower energy bills, better healthcare, more homes built for cheaper and faster, and having infrastructure that we can rely on.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The new Visuals feature generates images and 15-second videos that automatically sync with Suno songs.﻿.

The new Visuals feature generates images and 15-second videos that automatically sync with Suno songs.﻿.

It has been revealed that suno has introduced image and video generation in its latest effort to expand beyond being an AI music platform. The fresh feature, called “Visuals,” allows users to turn Suno songs into AI-generated video clips that automatically lipsync to lyrics, or make images via prompt descriptions that can be used as thumbnails and album artwork.

Visuals is available on web, iOS, and Android. The exact layout differs across Suno’s desktop and mobile interfaces, but users will find a fresh Visuals tab under Create mode on each version. Web users can also access Visuals by selecting the three dot menu on a song in their library. From there, users can select which section of the track to use, up to a maximum of 15 seconds, and select a reference image to build the generated video clip.

According to recent reports, there are three options available for the starting image reference: selecting one of the original character presets provided by Suno, uploading your own photo or artwork, or generating the image directly on Suno using descriptive prompts. The image generation capabilities also allow people to select specific aspect ratios, optimizing results for landscape or portrait modes and online platforms.

For video generation, users can select whether the reference image is used as the start or end frame, making it easier to edit the 15-second clips together. There’s a toggle to automatically lipsync vocals to the generated video, and tools for adjusting aspect ratio and clip length. Visuals also includes a dedicated video editing timeline for assembling clips into longer videos, and adding customizable song lyric text.

Recent findings suggest that the Visuals launch follows Suno introducing a Speech feature in October for generating spoken words and voiceovers. Adding video capabilities is another attempt to diversify the platform after Suno’s music generator attracted a number of high-profile lawsuits, though it seems some owners would rather the manufacturer focus on improving those song-generating capabilities. In the YouTube video for the Visuals launch, one user says “FIX AUDIO BEFORE ADDING CRAP NOBODY ASKED FOR” — a sentiment that other commenters are echoing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free access.

The decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in need, the premier of the island of Nevis has warned.

On Friday, Terrance Drew, the prime minister of the twin-island Caribbean nation, unveiled he would wind down the citizenship-by-investment (CBI) programme, after the European Union threatened to end visa-free access for St Kitts and Nevis.

Mark Brantley, the premier of Nevis, which has autonomous self-governance in some aspects, said he understood that the “country was given very little choice”, but did not “support the winding down of the program”.

Sources indicate that the 42-year-old CBI programme, which St Kitts and Nevis pioneered, allows wealthy foreigners to obtain citizenship and ultimately a passport by investing in infrastructure and other development projects. It has brought billions of dollars into the country and in some years accounted for the largest share of government revenue.

In June, the European Commission wrote to the five Caribbean nations that currently operate CBI programmes: St Kitts and Nevis, Dominica, Antigua and Barbuda, Grenada and St Lucia. It warned that countries may lose visa-free access to its 29-country Schengen area if they did not phase out CBI.

In Friday’s statement, Drew blamed concerns over the programme on mismanagement by previous administrations, including years of underselling to undercut other countries, a controversial prison project, weak escrow protections and investment sums not being properly paid into the citizenship unit.

In a recent development, he stated his government had led major reforms to the Caribbean’s programmes with international partners, including the US treasury, but argued that continuing the programme risked visa-free travel to parts of Europe and access to international banking. That could disrupt services allowing visitors to use overseas cards and families abroad to send money home.

Brantley, however, argued it was unfair for the EU to force St Kitts and Nevis to make a move without offering assistance to navigate the transition to other industries.

Sources indicate that “I have not yet seen from the EU any corresponding suggestions of assistance. And we have to realise that these citizenship-by-investment programs, not only in St Kitts and Nevis, but … smaller countries of the Caribbean, have contributed significantly to our gross domestic product and also to ensuring that our people … can get adequate access to water and to education, to healthcare and the like,” he stated.

Brantley described the 1 June 2028 deadline the EU gave the country to phase out the lucrative programme as “frankly ludicrous”.

In his statement, Drew mentioned the CBI programme “did a lot of good, but it also created a danger”.

According to recent reports, “When one source pays for half or more of everything, you are at its mercy. If it stops, everything stops. That is putting all of your eggs in one basket,” he added.

It has been revealed that the prime minister remarked the government aimed to diversify its economy by strengthening tourism, yachting, and digital and creative industries, among others. He added that the sale of clean, geothermal energy was “at the heart of it” with drilling and exploration already planned.

In a recent development, “I will not pretend that the road is easy. Less CBI money means we must spend wisely and plan carefully. We will. Our plan is to make this change by growing our economy. Raising taxes is not part of that plan,” Drew said.

Recent findings suggest that antigua and Barbuda has also expressed willingness to end the programme, though it is trying to negotiate a longer transition period. The five Caribbean governments have taken differing positions on the EU demand. According to local media, Grenada has indicated it wants its programme to continue until 2032, while Dominica and St Lucia have responded to Brussels without publicly committing to ending their programmes.

Jermine Abel in Basseterre contributed reporting.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Watch: BBC correspondents discuss historic Trump, Xi and Putin meeting.

Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met for the first time in more than a year on Wednesday, as they prepared for landmark talks in China with Xi Jinping.

The US president was greeted off his plane by the Chinese leader as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting between the pair and the Russian president.

After a carefully choreographed handshake and hug between Trump and Xi on the tarmac, the US president later greeted and exchanged pleasantries with Putin ahead of a reception.

Trump and Putin are expected to hold one-on-one talks on the sidelines of the summit on Thursday, in which the war in Ukraine could be discussed.

However the main focus during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum (Apec) will be on the US-China-Russia talks on Thursday - the first time the trio of leaders have met together in person.

A full agenda has not been made public but there have been various hints about what could be discussed, including the wars in Ukraine and Iran, nuclear proliferation, trade tensions and developments in artificial intelligence.

After a warm reception from Xi, the leaders of the US and Russia shook hands ahead of a reception.

It was not clear on Wednesday what form separate Trump-Putin talks would take, though a Kremlin spokesperson indicated short informal talks may happen without large delegations in the room.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has raised fears of a proposal to end the war being discussed in the absence of representatives from Kyiv or Europe.

Wednesday's handshake was the first in-person meeting between Trump and Putin since August 2025, when the Russian leader travelled to Alaska for talks on the Ukraine war which failed to deliver a breakthrough.

Xi's personal reception for Trump at the airport mimicked a similar move by the US president when the Chinese leader visited Washington in September, a gesture Xi described as "special".

In Shenzhen, a red carpet was rolled out in front of Air Force One for Trump, with a cheering crowd, honour guard, military flyover and flowers presentation all in place to welcome him.

Chinese state-run news agency Xinhua quoted Xi as saying he wanted to pursue a "constructive strategic and stable relationship based on respect, fairness, and equality".

Xi's greeting will be seen as a diplomatic gesture designed to begin the week's talks with his American counterpart on a cordial note.

A lavish welcome ceremony was laid on for Trump's arrival.

The south-east Chinese city the Apec summit is being held in is a booming area for manufacturing and advanced tech.

It comes against the backdrop of the ousting of Nvidia chief executing Jensen Huang, who admitted to having an affair with a woman suspected by US intelligence of spying for Beijing - a claim dismissed as a "smear" by China.

Trump has pursued warmer relations with China but the incident points to ongoing tensions between the two powers.

Several hours before Trump's arrival, Putin landed in Shenzhen and held around two hours of talks with Xi, with whom he has pressed for closer economic and defence relations.

Xi stated both countries would "move forward steadily and boldly" and that the relationship was "stable as a mountain, unshaken by storms".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite the turmoil at Nvidia following the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the manufacturer — as expected — delivered a solid quarter on Tuesday. More importantly, Nvidia reassured investors that its streak of record-breaking revenue won’t stop.

Sources indicate that on Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim CEO Colette Kress reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from the year-ago quarter and a beat above the company’s guidance. Nvidia had told Wall Street to expect $108 billion in revenue for its third quarter of fiscal 2027. Kress also projected an even bigger fourth quarter, with revenue expected to reach $130 billion, plus or minus 3%.

She also said full-year revenue is on track to exceed expectations.

In a recent development, “We are raising our fiscal year 2028 outlook. We expect revenue to grow approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% and off what is now a higher fiscal 2027 base,” Kress mentioned on the quarterly conference call on Tuesday. “Our outlook considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers’ access to capital.”.

Recent findings suggest that the firm also reminded investors that it was using some of its billions in cash to buy back shares. In September 2026, Nvidia increased its share buyback program by $150 billion. It spent $28.1 billion on its own shares during the quarter and still had another $227.3 billion remaining in the kitty for additional repurchases.

According to recent reports, ironically, Nvidia could also benefit from the plunge in its share price following Huang’s resignation last week, should shares remain depressed over the longer term. The stock is down about 10% since his departure. Investors, however, celebrated Tuesday’s quarterly results, sending shares up about 4% in after-hours trading.

Kress stressed that the organization was in good shape now and for the foreseeable future, even without Huang at the helm.

“We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap,” Kress stressed. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual. We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They’re all 100% behind us.”.

She added that the company has secured memory and advanced packaging capacity and is working with its chip manufacturer, TSMC, to “narrow the supply and demand gaps.”.

  • After traveling through the void of space for 49 years, Voyager 1 has hit a momentous milestone: The spacecraft is now officially 1 light-day away from Earth, which is, as NASA put it, “very, very far.” The probe crossed the milepost on Wednesday at 5:16AM ET and is now 16.094 billion miles away from our planet — equal to the distance that light travels in 24 hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s taken Voyager 1 almost 50 years to journey farther from Earth than light can travel in 24 hours.

It’s taken Voyager 1 almost 50 years to journey farther from Earth than light can travel in 24 hours.

After traveling through the void of space for 49 years, Voyager 1 has hit a momentous milestone: The spacecraft is now officially 1 light-day away from Earth, which is, as NASA put it, “very, very far.” The probe crossed the milepost on Wednesday at 5:16AM ET and is now 16.094 billion miles away from our planet — equal to the distance that light travels in 24 hours.

It’s the farthest that any human-made object has ever traveled, and Voyager 1’s journey isn’t over yet. It’s been heading toward a star called Gliese 445 in the Ursa Minor constellation since completing its primary objectives to conduct flybys of Jupiter and Saturn in 1980. That star is 17 light-years away, meaning Voyager 1 won’t pass by it for around 40,000 years, despite traveling at nearly 38,000 mph.

Recent findings suggest that the light-day milestone is a remarkable feat alone, but especially so when you consider that Voyager 1 is still operational. NASA has done well to keep it functioning, and it can continue to send back readings on plasma waves, magnetic fields, and space-bound particles, though it now takes radio signals an entire day to travel between Earth and the spacecraft. Voyager 2, which debuted 16 days before its twin, is also expected to reach a distance of 1 light-day away from Earth, but not until 2035.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Demonstrators tried to block vehicle carrying the baboons, whose capture authorities say is needed to protect both primate and human.
  • The relocation of a troop of baboons in Cape Town to a wildlife sanctuary has triggered furious protests by local people opposed to their capture, which officials argue is necessary to stop human-wildlife conflict in the city.
  • The 44-member Waterfall troop (named after the area they mainly inhabit) was captured in the southern seaside suburb of Simon’s Town on Friday and Saturday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Demonstrators tried to block vehicle carrying the baboons, whose capture authorities say is needed to protect both primate and human.

The relocation of a troop of baboons in Cape Town to a wildlife sanctuary has triggered furious protests by local people opposed to their capture, which officials argue is necessary to stop human-wildlife conflict in the city.

The 44-member Waterfall troop (named after the area they mainly inhabit) was captured in the southern seaside suburb of Simon’s Town on Friday and Saturday. A second, smaller Seaforth troop is also due to be moved.

It has been revealed that the growth in both baboon and human populations in Cape Town in recent years has led to increased conflict and more baboons dying as a result. Meanwhile, a heated debate has raged between people who believe that baboons and humans can coexist and those who argue that baboons in urban areas are in danger and in some cases need to be relocated. Some animal rights activists have compared authorities’ baboon management to apartheid.

Sources indicate that during Friday’s relocation, outraged protesters tried to stop vehicles taking the baboons away. One person sprayed a fire extinguisher, according to the Daily Maverick, a local news outlet.

After the confrontation, the local Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals branch urged those opposed to the baboons’ capture not to try to stop the vehicles. “Capture and transport are already stressful for the baboons,” it said in a statement. “Delaying their arrival prolongs their time in crates and risks adding to that stress – this is not fair on the baboons.”.

It said it remained opposed to the baboon’s relocation, adding: “Our presence did not imply support … our inspectors are present because the animals need someone looking out for them.”.

Industry observers note that on Sunday, dozens of people sat outside the wildlife centre in a silent protest, some tying flowers to the fence. Baboons from a different troop also gathered at the boundary, calling to the newly captive animals, the Daily Maverick reported.

“We stand together for the Seaforth and Waterfall troops, for their freedom, their dignity and their right to live as wild animals,” Mandy Neal, the administrator of the Save Kogelfontein Baboons Facebook group, posted on Monday, calling for weekly Sunday silent protests. “ Our message is simple: CAPTIVITY IS NOT CONSERVATION.”.

The City of Cape Town mentioned in a statement on Sunday that the relocation had been successful, with the baboons being monitored 24/7 after being checked by vets and the females receiving contraceptive implants.

It noted: “The Waterfall troop has been relocated due to the severity and persistence of human-baboon conflict in the Simon’s Town urban environment, the limited available natural low-lying habitat, the increasing risk to the baboons’ welfare, and public safety concerns … [and] as a very last resort after other interventions were evaluated and deemed ineffective, and as an alternative to culling.”.

It has been revealed that prof Justin O’Riain, a behavioural ecologist at the University of Cape Town, said the baboon management plan had undergone two years of public consultations. “It has thus been disappointing watching members of the public and select NGOs, many which did not engage in the stakeholder process, now compromising the safety and welfare of the baboons and people through violent actions directed at staff and baboons in transit.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: it revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday, up from the $22 billion reported in January.
  • The company invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it stated, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year.
  • But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang’s successor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, nvidia’s equity in private companies continues to grow: it revealed its stakes are now worth $65.5 billion on Tuesday, up from the $22 billion reported in January. The increase includes both new investments and significant markups of existing portfolio companies.

The company invested $16 billion into equities in the past quarter alone, it stated, and $58 billion in the past nine months of its fiscal year. This amount includes buying shares in public and private companies, yet it shows how the chipmaker made massive bets over the course of the year, especially compared to last year; in November 2025, the company reported spending $5 billion buying equity in the first nine months of that fiscal year.

But it’s unclear if this growth will continue under the interim CEO and Jensen Huang’s successor.

Industry observers note that nvidia stated in late 2023 that the goal of its corporate investing is to expand the AI ecosystem by backing startups it considers to be “game changers and market makers.”  Over the nearly three years that followed, the chipmaker has invested in nearly 350 startups, according to PitchBook. The companies Nvidia backed include Anthropic, OpenAI; neolabs like Thinking Machines and Reflection; neoclouds, like Lambda, Nscale, and Crusoe; as well as other companies developing AI infrastructure, robotics startups, and applications.

It’s also become a substantial financier of the data center build out, reporting $118 billion in guarantees with $105 billion of that the backstop it supplied for OpenAI’s $500 billion data center in Ohio.

According to recent reports, the organization made those commitments by allocating a meaningful portion of its excess cash flows. In Tuesday’s earning call, Kress mentioned Nvidia would continue providing financing assistance to strong customers and that “as the market matures and additional sources of capital become available,” the company would be “rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees.”.

But the question for the VC ecosystem is whether the manufacturer will continue to back startups at anywhere near the same level without Huang at the helm.

In a recent development, huang’s rampant dealmaking has reportedly been a source of concern for Kress. Investors have told TechCrunch that they anticipate that she will take a more conservative approach to startup investing, becoming more selective with fresh investments and writing smaller-sized checks into its existing portfolio companies.

“We intend to return all excess free cash flow net of strategic uses to shareholders during this last quarter and going forward,” Kress remarked on the earnings call on Tuesday. Just how strategic startups will be under her leadership, and under the future permanent CEO, remains to be seen. But for now, VCs are bracing for a meaningful pullback in capital.

Nigeria’s National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) mentioned a 28-year-old player named as Greene Da’monte Khiree from the state of Georgia was arrested at Lagos’s main airport last Wednesday after he arrived on a flight from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates.

The NDLEA said the player told them he had come to Nigeria to “build networks” for his basketball career. The agency said evidence on his phone suggested he had “knowledge of and involvement in the drug trafficking activity”. The NDLEA said it detained the player when he attempted to leave the airport with his hand luggage after abandoning two checked-in bags. The agency said those two bags were found to contain 32 parcels of marijuana, and a tracking device.

Nigeria has strict drug laws, and trafficking carries a sentence of life in prison.

A basketball player by the name of Damonte Greene is listed on the roster of the Pattani Raptors in the Thai Premier Men’s League. Greene, a Georgia native, played college basketball for Reinhardt University and South Georgia Technical College. He played semi-professional basketball in the US before representing a number of teams in Thailand.

It has been revealed that WNBA star Brittney Griner and former Utah State player Jarred Shaw were imprisoned in Russia and Indonesia respectively for marijuana offenses. Griner was released in December 2022, while Shaw remains in prison.

After former CEO Jensen Huang fought for US approval to sell H200 chips in China, Nvidia is now walking away.﻿.

It has been revealed that nvidia has stopped sending its advanced AI chips to China despite the approval it received from the White House to do so in December last year. The announcement was made by interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress during an earnings call on Tuesday, marking a notable shift for the company that, under former CEO Jensen Huang, fought for the right to ship its powerful Hopper architecture H200 chips to China.

Sources indicate that “Our guidance ⁠does not have any licensed Hopper data center products included, and we are no longer shipping ​licenced Hopper data center products to China,” Kress said. She did not explain why Nvidia was ceasing its H200 processor shipments or clarify whether Nvidia would pursue other business with China in the future.

The pivot comes after Huang stepped down from his position as Nvidia CEO last week following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, one with a woman who was suspected by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy. Nvidia already faced difficulties around offloading the AI chips prior to this scandal, however. Concerns were raised about failings to properly vet Chinese companies that were approved to handle the H200 AI chips. Reuters also reported earlier this month that around 600,000 ⁠H200 chips ​were stuck in Hong Kong after Beijing withheld approval for large-scale imports, with China seeking to reduce its dependency on US technology.

Sources indicate that president Trump, Xi Jinping of China and Vladimir V. Putin of Russia greeted each other with smiles and handshakes on Wednesday in Shenzhen, China, hours after Mr. Trump received a personal welcome from Mr. Xi at the Chinese city’s airport that included a hug.

Recent findings suggest that the indicates of friendliness by the three world leaders, on the eve of a trilateral summit, contrasted sharply with their divergent stances on some of the world’s most pressing issues, including nuclear arms control, China’s ability to access advanced A.I. chips and the future of the war in Ukraine.

On Thursday, the presidents are expected to participate in the first-ever trilateral gathering of the leaders of the United States, China and Russia, when at least some of those concerns could be on the agenda. The summit will cap Mr. Trump’s whirlwind trip to Asia, which has been shadowed by the Nvidia scandal, trade conflicts and critical infrastructure breakdowns at home.

Earlier, Mr. Xi met Mr. Trump at the airport in Shenzhen, something he did not do when Mr. Trump visited Beijing in May. But Mr. Trump made a point of going to Joint Base Andrews outside Washington to greet Mr. Xi in September, an uncommon move for an American president and the first time Mr. Trump had done so for a foreign visitor. In effect, Mr. Xi returned the gesture.

The red-carpet greeting on the tarmac — with a crowd of people in colorful costumes waving flags and flowers and chanting “warm welcome” in Mandarin — came shortly after Mr. Xi met with Mr. Putin, who arrived earlier in the day. The Chinese leader had sent a lower-ranking official to greet Mr. Putin but used their subsequent meeting to hail the Chinese-Russian relationship as “steadfast as a rock through wind and rain.”.

In a recent development, the two encounters underscored Mr. Xi’s efforts to balance relations with Russia and the United States. While Russia has become a close partner in recent years and Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin have developed a bond, China has a far more extensive economic relationship with the United States.

Mr. Trump will also meet separately with Mr. Xi on Thursday, his third encounter this year with the Chinese leader after he visited Beijing in the spring and the lavish state visit at the White House a couple months ago. Although Mr. Trump once regularly lashed out at China over its trade practices, he has become more intent on forging friendly ties between the world’s two largest economies.

In a recent development, the visit, however, may have a see-no-evil, hear-no-evil quality because Mr. Trump has said he does not intend to raise challenges of Chinese interference in American affairs. The chief executive of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, was forced to resign last week after revelations of an extramarital affair with a businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence determined was spying for China. But Mr. Trump has said he will not discuss the matter with Mr. Xi.

No relationship has proved more critical for Mr. Putin than his bond with Mr. Xi. Recent findings suggest that president Vladimir V. Putin of Russia touched down in Asia in recent hours. So did two of his nuclear-capable bombers.

Mr. Putin arrived early Wednesday in Shenzhen, China, for a regional economic meeting and a trilateral summit with President Trump and President Xi Jinping of China. Russia lags both China and the United States significantly in economic output, technological innovation, population size and trade flows, making Mr. Putin’s participation in the trilateral summit scheduled for Thursday to some degree conspicuous.

But the one critical area where Russia has retained its lead is in nuclear weapons. Russia boasts the world’s biggest nuclear arsenal, which Mr. Putin has brandished as a reason the world must continue to accord Moscow a certain level of deference and respect. Russia has also developed a range of new nuclear weapons systems in recent years.

The Tu-95MS is a nuclear-capable bomber with intercontinental range. Russia has also deployed the bombers in its war against Ukraine to launch conventional missiles.

Russia and Vietnam have a longstanding relationship that dates back to the Cold War, and Russia still supplies the vast majority of Vietnam’s military equipment.

For Vietnam, the decision to welcome the Russian nuclear bombers demonstrates China that Vietnamese leaders have a range of possible military partners to push back against any aggressive moves by Beijing. Vietnam has also deepened its ties with the United States in recent years.
